sources.note: Three(later four)-level epistemic hierarchy: Proposition (semantic content) subset-of Assertion (proposition + epistemic commitment/evidence/provenance) subset-of Knowledge (justified assertion), with a correction that KnowledgeOS can only ever reach a Truth Assessment, never absolute Truth/Reality itself.

rows.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
rows.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.
invariants: Every Assertion contains a Proposition but not every Proposition is an Assertion
Every Knowledge contains an Assertion but not every Assertion is Knowledge

lineage_claims.quote: Our Knowledge Atom is actually an Assertion, not a Proposition.

rows.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
rows.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.
invariants: KnowledgeOS maintains epistemically justified knowledge, not an absolute oracle of Truth

lineage_claims.quote: I would change one thing: don't make Truth an internal primitive yet

rows.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
rows.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

rows.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
rows.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

rows.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
rows.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

rows.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
rows.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

rows.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
rows.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

rows.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
rows.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

rows.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
rows.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

rows.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
rows.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

rows.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
rows.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

rows.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
rows.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.
missing: the domain authority's decision on both open points

rows.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
rows.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

rows.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
rows.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

rows.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
rows.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

rows.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
rows.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

rows.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
rows.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

rows.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
rows.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

lineage_claims.target: an earlier equation 'Assertion = Knowledge' used previously in the theory
lineage_claims.quote: We previously used: Assertion = Knowledge. Too strong.

rows.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
rows.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

rows.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
rows.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

rows.anchor: LogicalValidity \neq EmpiricalTruth
rows.statement: States Conclusion≠Truth as fundamental: even Γ⊨P only means P follows from Γ under the specified formal system, not that the premises describe reality correctly, giving LogicalValidity≠EmpiricalTruth — 'one of the most important mathematical safeguards in the architecture'. Worked compliance example distinguishes Proposition A (Nexus.version=3.69, a factual claim supported by runtime/DB/LLM evidence E_1,E_2,E_3) from Proposition B (does production Nexus satisfy the required version), where an architecture document stating 'required>=3.85' is used as a NORMATIVE CONSTRAINT combined with runtime evidence (3.69), NOT as evidence that Nexus actually runs 3.85 — 'the architecture document was not evidence that Nexus was 3.85; it was a normative constraint used together with runtime evidence'. This yields EpistemicCorrectness ≠ DomainAdequacy: KnowledgeOS can know something accurately (well-supported Nexus.version=3.69) while that thing is undesirable (violates the >=3.85 requirement) — the discrepancy is 'the current state is well-supported but does not satisfy the ideal constraint', not 'evidence says Nexus is wrong'.

rows.anchor: NoObservation \neq EvidenceOfAbsence
rows.statement: Poses two explicit design decisions before freezing the model: Decision A — can absence-of-result count as evidence of absence (e.g. an API query returning no repository named 'foo')? Recommendation: NO in general — NoObservation≠EvidenceOfAbsence unless the observation mechanism is sufficiently complete to justify the negative inference (a complete authoritative DB query may justify it; an incomplete internet search may not). Decision B — should KnowledgeOS support Bayesian probability P(H|E) as the fundamental epistemic model? Recommendation: NO — a qualitative/structural epistemic model should be the foundation, with Bayesian/statistical/fuzzy/domain-specific models as PLUGGABLE inference policies, keeping the mathematical architecture general.
missing: the domain authority's decision on both points

rows.anchor: EVD-1: Evidence is relational ... EVD-11: No scalar confidence value may replace the underlying evidence structure.
rows.statement: Freezes eleven Evidence axioms EVD-1..11: (1) Evidence is relational; (2) grounded in observation/provenance; (3) proposition-relative; (4) evidence quality is multidimensional; (5) evidence comparison is context/policy-dependent; (6) independent evidence must be distinguished from repeated evidence; (7) contradictory evidence is preserved, not silently discarded; (8) evidence does not imply truth; (9) conclusion requires an explicit inference rule; (10) every conclusion must be traceable to its premises and provenance; (11, 'the most important') no scalar confidence value may replace the underlying evidence structure. States the deepest principle reached: 'KnowledgeOS does not compute Truth directly. It computes a traceable epistemic state from observations and evidence under explicit rules': K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,Observations,Evidence,Rules,Context), with every conclusion traceable backward Conclusion->InferenceRule->Evidence->Observation->Artifact->Source. A 13-row closure-status table marks Artifact/SourceObservation/CandidateProposition/EvidenceRelation as Closed, EvidenceQuality/EvidenceComparison as closed-as-model-but-policy-dependent, EvidenceAggregation as needing formal policy families, Deductive inference as computationally closed, Inductive/Abductive as computable-but-policy-dependent, Conclusion as closed-as-structured-object, and Truth as explicitly 'not computationally guaranteed'.

rows.anchor: I have read DeepSeek's proposed **Computational Closure 3 — Evidence**.
rows.statement: Explicit corpus provenance detail: one section is attributed by name to 'DeepSeek' proposing its own Computational Closure 3 - Evidence (E=(P,S,R,T,Q,Π,C), relation types Supports/Contradicts/Contextualizes/Qualifies, quality tuple Q=(Reliability,Relevance,Currency,Independence,Completeness)), which is then reviewed by a distinct 'senior mathematician and DDD architect' voice — direct evidence that this strand of the corpus involved cross-model critique and revision cycles (at least two different AI systems contributing competing formalizations of the same closure).

lineage_claims.target: S0847's Evidence formalization (same tuple E=(P,S,R,T,Q,Π,C) and eleven test cases), here explicitly attributed to a named external model 'DeepSeek'
lineage_claims.quote: I have read DeepSeek's proposed Computational Closure 3 — Evidence.

rows.anchor: ER(O,P,R,C,\Pi,\tau)
rows.statement: Corrects DeepSeek's Evidence tuple E=(P,S,R,T,Q,Π,C) — treating Evidence as if intrinsic to an observation — to an EvidentialRelation ER(O,P,R,C,Π,τ), since the same observation ('Nexus API returned 3.69') supports P_1 (Nexus.version=3.69) but not P_2 (Nexus.isSecure): Observation × Proposition × Rule -> EvidentialRelation. Also corrects the four relation types (Supports/Contradicts/Contextualizes/Qualifies) as an incomplete, non-extensible vocabulary: 'Supports' alone splits into direct/indirect/deductive/corroborative/probabilistic/abductive support, and 'Contradicts' splits into logical/empirical/normative/domain-rule incompatibility — recommending EvidentialRelationType be extensible and rule-governed (basic vocabulary SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS/QUALIFIES/CONTEXTUALIZES/CORROBORATES/DERIVED_FROM/DEPENDS_ON, but not treated as equivalent mathematical categories).

lineage_claims.target: DeepSeek's Evidence tuple E=(P,S,R,T,Q,Π,C) and its four-value relation-type enum
lineage_claims.quote: The fundamental object is not really Evidence but an evidential relation.

rows.anchor: Evidence \neq Assessment \neq Inference
rows.statement: Argues DeepSeek's declaration 'the Evidence boundary is computationally closed' is premature: its Σ_A=Assess({E_1,...,E_n},Rules,Context) is only a function SIGNATURE, not a defined semantics — it doesn't specify what happens when Q(E_1)>Q(E_2) but E_1 supports P and E_2 contradicts P (accept P? mark conflict-active? provisional? unresolved?). Separates three distinct mathematical layers that must not be conflated: Layer 1 Evidence (O --P,C,R--> ER), Layer 2 Evidence Assessment ({ER_1,...,ER_n} --ρ--> Σ_E), Layer 3 Inference (Γ --Rule--> Conclusion) — Evidence ≠ Assessment ≠ Inference, called 'probably the most important refinement'. Grades the original proposal ~85% architecturally mature but only 60-70% mathematically closed.

rows.anchor: What properties must `AssessEvidence()` satisfy so that KnowledgeOS behaves predictably when evidence is added, removed, duplicated, contradicted, or reinterpreted?
rows.statement: Reframes evidence-assessment design around laws-first rather than formula-first: defines EA=(S^+,S^-,Q,U,D,C_f,Π) as a structured (non-collapsed) result preserving Support(P) and Support(¬P) simultaneously, and requires A_ρ(E_P,C)->EA explicitly NOT to yield P directly (assessment does not establish truth).

rows.anchor: A(\{e\}) \approx A(\{e,e\})
rows.statement: Law E4 Duplicate Idempotence: adding an exact duplicate of existing evidence must not create additional independent evidential support, A({e})≈A({e,e}) — otherwise 'an attacker could simply submit the same observation 1000 times and manufacture confidence'. Law E5 distinguishes this from genuine corroboration: IndependentCorroboration ≠ DuplicateEvidence — two genuinely independent sources supporting P (e.g. a database and a separate monitoring system) SHOULD generally increase support relative to either alone, provided the policy recognizes both as relevant and reliable.

rows.anchor: Adding\ supporting\ evidence \text{ cannot reduce support for }P
rows.statement: Law E6 corrects a naive monotonicity requirement (E⊆E' ⇒ Support(E)≤Support(E')) as NOT universally valid, since new evidence may contradict existing evidence (adding ¬P-evidence to a P-supported set should not increase Support(P)). Replaces it with signed/conditional monotonicity: adding supporting evidence cannot reduce support for P; adding contradicting evidence cannot reduce support for ¬P; but overall epistemic uncertainty may still increase. Law E7 Conflict Preservation: Support(P)>0 ∧ Support(¬P)>0 ⇒ ConflictInformation≠∅ — the weaker side must never be silently discarded, so KnowledgeOS can say 'the strongest evidence currently supports P, but contrary evidence exists' rather than flatly 'P=true'.

lineage_claims.target: a naive unconditional monotonicity requirement E⊆E' ⇒ Support(E)≤Support(E')
lineage_claims.quote: But that is not universally valid. ... Therefore we need signed monotonicity.

rows.anchor: A_\rho(E,C_1) \neq A_\rho(E,C_2)
rows.statement: Law E8 Context Sensitivity (A_ρ(E,C_1)≠A_ρ(E,C_2) is not an error — e.g. 'Nexus 3.69' may suffice for 'what was installed yesterday?' but not for 'is Nexus ready for migration?') and Law E9 Policy Sensitivity (A_ρ1(E,C)≠A_ρ2(E,C) may legitimately occur — a security-critical policy requiring official-source/freshness<24h/independent-confirmation vs an operational-inventory policy accepting a single trusted DB with freshness<30 days can validly reach different epistemic statuses from the same evidence: 'policy relativism within a stable mathematical framework'). Law E10 Assessment≠Inference (EA≠Conclusion; Conclusion=Infer(EA,R,C)) and Law E11 Assessment≠Truth (EA=VeryStrong ⇏ P=True: StrongEvidence(P) ⇏ Truth(P) — 'the system represents the epistemic position of the Knower; it does not magically acquire metaphysical access to reality'). Law E12 Reproducibility: (E,C,ρ)⇒EA and (EA,R,C)⇒Conclusion must be deterministic given fixed inputs.

rows.anchor: Deduplication/Dependency\ Analysis \prec Aggregation
rows.statement: Tests S0848's WeightedStrength/logarithmic-aggregate formula against the twelve laws: the log-dampened denominator changes when a duplicate is added (n->n+1), which prevents unlimited linear growth but does NOT solve the underlying identity/dependency problem, since it treats duplicates as merely 'more' evidence rather than recognizing e_i∼e_j (evidentially identical/dependent) before aggregating. Establishes the required architectural ordering: Deduplication/Dependency Analysis ≺ Aggregation — dependency/equivalence analysis must occur strictly before aggregation, not be approximated by a dampening factor within it.

lineage_claims.target: S0848's WeightedStrength/AggregateSupport formula as a sufficient solution to evidence dependency
lineage_claims.quote: That is actually good in one sense ... but it does not solve the fundamental duplication problem.

rows.anchor: E \xrightarrow{Normalize} E^* \xrightarrow{DependencyAnalysis} G_E \xrightarrow{QualityAssessment} Q_E \xrightarrow{Aggregation} EA \xrightarrow{Inference} Conclusion
rows.statement: Revises the assessment pipeline to explicitly sequence Normalize -> DependencyAnalysis (building the evidence graph G_E) -> QualityAssessment (Q_E) -> Aggregation (EA) -> Inference (Conclusion), 'significantly stronger than the current DeepSeek model'. Proposes three clean bounded contexts: Evidence Context (Observation, EvidentialRelation, EvidenceGraph), Assessment Context (QualityAssessment, DependencyAnalysis, EvidenceAssessment, AssessmentPolicy), Reasoning Context (InferenceRule, Inference, Conclusion) — Evidence | Assessment | Reasoning, 'much cleaner than a generic epistemology module'. Proposes a twelve-case test universe (duplicate, independent corroboration, dependent corroboration, contradiction, unequal reliability, stale, irrelevant, incomplete, incomparable, policy change, context change, evidence removal) to test any candidate aggregation function against the twelve laws before choosing among weighted-deterministic, Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, possibility-theoretic, ordinal, or hybrid evidence-combination models — noting this can be derived and tested directly from the formal requirements without external research.

rows.anchor: e=(o,p,r,c,\pi,\tau)
rows.statement: Defines the evidence universe precisely: 𝒪 observations, 𝒫 propositions, 𝒞 contexts, ℛ rules, ℰ evidential relations with each e=(o,p,r,c,π,τ) so ℰ⊆𝒪×𝒫×ℛ×𝒞×Π×T. Reduces the earlier four-valued relation-type vocabulary (Supports/Contradicts/Contextualizes/Qualifies) to a three-valued core Polarity(e)∈{+,-,0} (supports P / supports ¬P / neither), keeping richer relation metadata (qualifies, contextualizes) as separate annotations rather than forcing them into polarity — giving E_P^+ and E_P^- as the supporting/contradicting evidence sets, 'a mathematically clean representation of contradictory evidence'.

lineage_claims.quote: For the core calculus, I recommend starting with just: Polarity(e) ∈ {+,-,0}.

rows.anchor: N:\mathcal E\rightarrow\mathcal E^*
rows.statement: Defines a Normalize operator N:ℰ->ℰ* that must run BEFORE assessment, identifying exact duplicates, semantic duplicates, derived duplicates, superseded observations, invalid provenance, irrelevant evidence, and temporal incompatibilities — worked example: DB->LLM-reads-DB->Document-copies-DB-result should collapse to one evidence contribution e_1 with e_2,e_3 recorded as dependent on it, not three independent contributions. Non-collapsed assessment output EA=(S^+,S^-,U,D,Q,Γ): structured support for P, structured support for ¬P, uncertainty, dependency/corroboration info, quality assessment, qualifications/limitations — deliberately not EA=0.87.

rows.anchor: E-1 — Duplicate Invariance ... E-8 — Assessment ≠ Conclusion
rows.statement: Freezes eight candidate KnowledgeOS mathematical laws E-1..E-8: Duplicate Invariance (e≡e' ⇒ A(E)=A(E∪{e'}) for independent contribution); Corroboration (independent supporting evidence may be recognized as additional support); Dependency Preservation (dependent evidence cannot be treated as independent corroboration); Contradiction Preservation (both-sided support retained, conflict information kept); Context Relativity; Policy Relativity; Assessment≠Truth (EA(P) ⇏ P=True); Assessment≠Conclusion (EA≠Conclusion). States the explicit dependency ordering Normalize ≺ DependencyAnalysis ≺ QualityAssessment ≺ Aggregation ≺ Inference as an architectural invariant: 'you cannot safely aggregate evidence before determining whether the evidence is duplicated or dependent' — worked example: Database->LLM->Report->Manager presentation LOOKS like four sources but is epistemically one underlying observation with three transformations.

rows.anchor: I ran the experiment as a small executable epistemic model, using the 10 evidence cases we defined.
rows.statement: Reports an actually-executed simulation (results delivered as a downloadable CSV) of a 10-case evidence universe: (1) duplicate evidence — Assess({e1})=Assess({e1,e2}) held, confirming duplicates cannot manufacture support; (2) independent corroboration (an independent monitoring system corroborating the API) — Assess(e1,e3)>Assess(e1), confirming Corroboration≠Duplication; (3) LLM-derived evidence explicitly marked as derived from the API observation — correctly NOT counted as independent corroboration (e_4 ⊥̸ e_1); (4) stale evidence — retained in the graph but its contribution diminished by low Currency, confirming Stale≠Deleted; (5) irrelevant evidence (an ADR mentioning Nexus but not relevant to the version proposition, Relevance=0.05) — effectively no contribution, confirming Evidence existence≠Evidence relevance; (6) contradictory evidence (3.70 vs 3.69) — both Support(P) and Support(¬P) preserved simultaneously with Conflict=ACTIVE, Resolution=OPEN, rather than the system picking a winner and discarding the other observation.

experiment.hypothesis: A dependency-aware evidence assessment model satisfying laws E-1..E-8 correctly handles duplication, corroboration, LLM-derived dependency, staleness, irrelevance, and contradiction without manufacturing false confidence or discarding conflicting evidence.
experiment.setup: A small executable epistemic model implementing Normalize->DependencyAnalysis->QualityAssessment->Aggregation over a 10-evidence test universe (direct observation, duplicate, independent corroboration, dependent LLM output, stale observation, irrelevant observation, contradictory observation, weak source, authoritative source, derived mathematical conclusion) concerning the proposition Nexus.version=3.69.
experiment.assumptions: Uses a specific scoring function s(e)=Reliability×Relevance×Currency×Independence and a saturating aggregation 1-∏(1-s_i), explicitly flagged as an unvalidated engineering choice, not derived from the theory.
experiment.inputs: Ten named evidence cases (see statement) plus their quality/dependency annotations.
experiment.method: Run the implemented assessment pipeline over the ten cases and check outputs against the eight laws.
experiment.result: All tested laws held for the six illustrated cases (duplicate invariance, corroboration, dependency detection, staleness retention, irrelevance near-zero contribution, contradiction preservation).
experiment.interpretation: The dependency-first architecture (Normalize before Aggregate) is empirically validated as necessary; the specific numeric formula used is not yet validated as correct or unique.
experiment.limitations: Only 6 of the 10 defined cases are discussed in detail in this document; the scoring formula itself is not derived from the axioms and is flagged as a placeholder; results are reported qualitatively in-document (full data in an external, unreadable-from-here CSV artifact).
experiment.conclusion: Proceed to a comparative experiment testing multiple candidate evidence-combination algebras (Max, Weighted Mean, Probabilistic, Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, Ordinal, hybrid) against the same law set before selecting one for KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: \textbf{Structured Evidence Calculus} + \textbf{Pluggable Inference Mathematics}
rows.statement: Final architectural recommendation: KnowledgeOS core mathematics defines Evidence, Provenance, Dependency, Polarity, Quality, Conflict, Assessment as a Structured Evidence Calculus, but does NOT dictate one universal numerical aggregation theory; individual policies (ρ_deterministic, ρ_bayesian, ρ_statistical, ρ_ruleBased, etc.) implement domain-specific combination rules as Pluggable Inference Mathematics — 'analogous to DDD: the domain defines the invariants; policies implement domain-specific decisions.'

rows.anchor: \text{Aggregation}\neq\text{Inference}
rows.statement: Reiterates three distinct layers before testing: Layer 1 Evidence representation e=(P,π,ρ,κ,τ,δ,...) (proposition, provenance, polarity/relation, quality, context/time, dependency); Layer 2 Evidence aggregation ⊕_ρ; Layer 3 Inference Γ⊢_ρP or P(H|E) — Aggregation≠Inference, since e.g. Bayesian inference is 'a much richer inferential framework', not merely an alternative score formula, so the four candidates (Max/Weighted Mean/Saturating/Bayesian) should not all be called 'evidence algebras' in exactly the same sense.

rows.anchor: Evidence\ does\ not\ own\ Truth ... LLM\ does\ not\ own\ Truth ... Inference\ does\ not\ own\ Evidence
rows.statement: Proposes four bounded contexts with explicit ownership: Evidence context (Evidence, Observation, Provenance, Dependency, Polarity, EvidenceQuality, EvidenceAssessment); Conflict context (Conflict, ConflictRule, ConflictStatus, ResolutionReference); Reasoning context (InferenceRule, InferencePolicy, Inference, Conclusion); Knowledge State context (Assertion, KnowledgeState, StateTransition, Coherence). Three ownership-exclusion invariants: Evidence does not own Truth; LLM does not own Truth; Inference does not own Evidence — each context has a distinct, non-overlapping responsibility.

rows.anchor: E | evidence? epistemic state? | NEITHER — Entity ... D | data? domain? dimension? | Dimension ... V | validation? | NO — Value
rows.statement: All three of mandate §7's suspicions about P=(E,D,V) are resolved against the intuitive readings, per question-14 (2026-08-26): E is NEITHER evidence nor epistemic state but Entity ('anything that can be the subject of knowledge'); D is NEITHER data nor domain but Dimension ('a semantic axis of variation or classification', with domain being a field of D, not D itself); V is NOT validation but Value ('a specific position on a dimension'); Evidence itself has its own separate symbol E_v in the same table.

rows.anchor: Entity E | element of ℰ | primitive ... Dimension D | (ID, Name, ValueSpace, Type, Domain) | primitive, but structured ... Value V | element of V_D | derived from D ... Proposition P | (E,D,V) | derived
rows.statement: Full specification table for the four objects: Entity (primitive, element of the entity universe, membership decidable), Dimension (primitive but structured as (ID,Name,ValueSpace,Type,Domain), admits(v) decidable), Value (derived from its Dimension — has no meaning without it, membership in V_D decidable), Proposition (derived triple (E,D,V), WellFormed decidable) — all four are observable and all four participate inside every assertion as content/operand.

rows.anchor: D_VER = Dimension("Version", ("3.68","3.69","3.70"), scale="ordinal") ... T: assert (Nexus, Version, "9.99") -> REJECTED(structure): V∉V_D
rows.statement: WellFormed(P) is executed as a real transformation-boundary rejection (in a separate artifact H), not decorative: a Version dimension with value-space {3.68,3.69,3.70} rejects an out-of-range assertion (Nexus,Version,'9.99') with REJECTED(structure): V not in V_D; this predicate only became meaningful once P was formally defined, since 'ill-formed' had no prior meaning.

experiment.hypothesis: WellFormed(P) is a real, enforceable structural gate
experiment.setup: D_VER dimension with value space {3.68,3.69,3.70}, scale=ordinal
experiment.assumptions: WellFormed(P) checks V in V_D
experiment.method: evaluate WellFormed on both
experiment.result: P1 WellFormed=True; the 9.99 assertion is REJECTED(structure)
experiment.interpretation: WellFormed(P) genuinely rejects real ill-typed input at the transformation boundary
experiment.limitations: executed in a separate artifact (H), not shown inline here
experiment.conclusion: ENGINEERINGALLY VERIFIED

rows.anchor: Q14 §3.4 classifies value-space types as Nominal / Ordinal / Interval / Ratio ... But Q14 gives version numbers as its example of an INTERVAL scale. That is wrong ... Version is ORDINAL at best.
rows.statement: Measurement-theory correction contesting the corpus: question-14 correctly attaches Nominal/Ordinal/Interval/Ratio scale typing to the Dimension (not the Value), but wrongly classifies version numbers as Interval — 3.69-3.68 has no meaningful unit-magnitude, version ordering is not numeric ordering (3.10 > 3.9 as versions but 3.10 < 3.9 as decimals), and Interval requires equal intervals to mean equal differences, which versions lack; version scale is Ordinal at best, and since Nexus.Version is the corpus's most-used worked example, an inadmissible-arithmetic hazard sits inside the canonical illustration — explicit VERIFIER RECOMMENDATION contesting the corpus.

rows.anchor: JUSTIFIED AND RETAINED. It is not rejected. ... (E,D) is a natural bucketing key, which reduces contradiction detection from O(n²) to O(n + Σᵢbᵢ²).
rows.statement: Verdict: P=(E,D,V) is JUSTIFIED AND RETAINED — it survives every §7 test (each symbol typed; two primitive one derived; all observable and computable; well-formedness decidable and executed; participates in both K as assertion content and T as operand; carries measurement discipline no rival carries); a concrete engineering payoff is identified — (E,D) is a natural bucketing key reducing contradiction detection from O(n^2) to O(n + sum_i b_i^2), unavailable while P was opaque.

rows.anchor: What is NOT justified: the eleven rival formulations ((V_P,E_P), (L,μ), (S,ρ,O,Γ), (E,≺), (V,E_P), Proposition = Subject, proposition = assertion). (S,R,O) is an isomorphic rename and is subsumed rather than rejected.
rows.statement: Eleven rival proposition formulations are explicitly found NOT justified relative to P=(E,D,V): (V_P,E_P), (L,mu), (S,rho,O,Gamma), (E,precedes), (V,E_P), Proposition=Subject, proposition=assertion, and others; one candidate, (S,R,O), is treated differently — an isomorphic rename of (E,D,V), hence subsumed rather than rejected.

rows.anchor: E and V are each doubly bound in the corpus — E = Entity (Q14) and Events (025x); V = Value (Q14) and Vertices (207). A terminology defect, not a formal gap. Recorded in artifact J.
rows.statement: Residual defect: the symbols E and V are each overloaded elsewhere in the corpus — E means both Entity (question-14) and Events (file 025x); V means both Value (question-14) and Vertices (step 207) — classified as a terminology defect rather than a formal gap, and recorded separately in artifact J.

rows.anchor: K = (𝒜, ℛ) ; 𝒜 = Set(Assertion) Assertion = (id, P, e, c, t, Π) ; P = (E, D, V) ... ℛ = ℛ_sup ⊎ ℛ_ref ⊎ ℛ_der ⊎ ℛ_supp ⊎ ℛ_res ⊎ ℛ_rel ; DAGs: sup, ref, der non-transitive: supp, res symmetric: rel ; DERIVED, never stored: Σ · equals · contradicts · conflictsWith ; EXTERNAL: History · Policy · Autho
rows.statement: The canonical statement of the whole artifact: K=(A,R) with A a set of Assertion=(id,P,e,c,t,Pi) where P=(E,D,V), e a subset of Evidence=(ref,polarity,state), c in Context, t a half-open interval [vf,vt), Pi in Origin; R is a disjoint union of six relation kinds (supersedes, references, derived_from, supports, restricts/res, related_to) with sup/ref/der required to be DAGs, supp/res non-transitive, and rel symmetric; Sigma (epistemic status), equals, contradicts and conflictsWith are DERIVED and never stored; History, Policy, Authority, and Gamma are EXTERNAL to K.

rows.anchor: The third rejection is only possible because P = (E,D,V) is defined. Before CB-2 closed, an ill-formed proposition could not be detected, because "ill-formed" had no meaning. Closing the proposition gap directly strengthened the transformation guard — a concrete downstream payoff.
rows.statement: The out-of-range-value rejection is possible only because the Proposition P=(E,D,V) formalization was closed (CB-2): before that, 'ill-formed' had no formal meaning, so the transformation guard could not detect it — a concrete downstream engineering payoff of resolving the proposition-type question.

rows.anchor: 1 CONTEXT ... 2 OBSERVATION ... EVIDENCE ... 3 DIMENSION ... PROPOSITION ... 4 ASSERTION ... 5 IDENTITY ... 6 T: assert A1 -> ok |𝒜|=1 ... 7 T: relate(intern) -> REJECTED(authority) ... 8 T: cycle attempt -> REJECTED(structure) ... 9 INVARIANTS ... 10 ASSESSMENT ... FINAL STATE |𝒜|=4 |ℛ|=1 Semantica
rows.statement: A single continuous ten-step executed run builds Context, Observation/Evidence (held by reference per ADR-T16), Dimension/Proposition (with WellFormed check), four concrete Assertions, an identity check (A1 != A3 despite the same proposition, differing only in context), four successful assert transformations, an authority-gated relate (one rejected, one accepted), two structural rejections (a supersedes cycle attempt and an ill-formed value), a full invariant check (StructuralValid, SemanticallyValid, acyclicity, three differently-explained contradiction checks), and five Assessment calls — ending in a final state of |A|=4, |R|=1, SemanticallyValid=True.

experiment.hypothesis: a complete Knowledge State lifecycle (construct/transform/compare/assess/invariant-check) can be executed end to end from primitive inputs
experiment.setup: concrete Nexus-version context/observation/evidence/dimension/proposition/assertion objects
experiment.assumptions: the artifact D/E canonical K=(A,R) and T models

experiment.method: sequential execution of the ten steps, each producing real program output
experiment.result: all ten steps succeed with the expected outcomes, ending in a semantically valid 4-assertion, 1-relation state
experiment.interpretation: the canonical theory is not merely conceptually coherent but mechanically executable end to end
experiment.limitations: executes the theory's own reference implementation, not a real KnowledgeOS bounded context

rows.anchor: 3 | WellFormed(P) is a real gate. scale=ordinal — my correction to Q14's "version = interval"
rows.statement: Restates and re-executes, in the end-to-end run, the earlier measurement-theory correction (version scale is ordinal, not interval, contra Q14) as a live WellFormed(P) gate.

lineage_claims.quote: 3 | WellFormed(P) is a real gate. scale=ordinal — my correction to Q14's "version = interval"

rows.anchor: 5 | same proposition ≠ same assertion — a theorem, executed
rows.statement: Line 5 of the run executes the theorem same-proposition != same-assertion concretely: A1 and A3 share the same proposition P1=(Nexus,Version,3.69) but differ in context (production vs staging), and are confirmed distinct assertions (A1 != A3 = True).

rows.anchor: Every Assertion contains a Proposition, but not every Proposition is an Assertion. ... P does not by itself tell us who asserted it; when it was valid; in what context; what evidence supports it; how it originated. Those belong to the assertion layer.
rows.statement: Proposition (semantic content) is formally distinguished from Assertion (id,P,e,c,t,Pi): every Assertion contains a Proposition but not every Proposition is an Assertion; a bare proposition like 'Nexus uses version 3.69' does not by itself carry asserter, validity period, context, evidence, or origin.

rows.anchor: What must be proven: Type validity ... Semantic well-formedness ... Identity ... Expressiveness ... Closure ... Non-redundancy
rows.statement: Six proof obligations are set for P=(E,D,V) to become a formal proposition type: type validity (E in E-universe, D in D-universe, V in V_D), semantic well-formedness WellFormed(E,D,V), an identity criterion (whether P1=P2 is structural or semantic), expressiveness (representing all propositions KnowledgeOS requires), closure (operations over propositions return valid propositions), and non-redundancy (whether E,D,V are each individually necessary).

rows.anchor: Suppose we remove E. Then P=(D,V). ... entity identity cannot generally be reconstructed from D,V. Hence E is necessary. ... Remove D. Then P=(E,V). ... D is necessary to type the value's semantic role. ... Remove V. Then P=(E,D). This says: Nexus has a Version. It does not say: Nexus has version 3.
rows.statement: A three-way structural (argued, not executed) removal test supports P=(E,D,V)'s minimality: removing Entity leaves (D,V)=(Version,3.69), which cannot determine which of many possible entities (Nexus, GitLab, Java, ...) it concerns; removing Dimension leaves (E,V)=(Nexus,3.69), which cannot determine what semantic role 3.69 plays (version? risk score? capacity?); removing Value leaves (E,D)=(Nexus,Version), which asserts only that Nexus has A version, not which one — each removal loses distinct information, giving P=(E,D,V) strong minimality support while explicitly noting a full executed counterexample would strengthen the claim further.
missing: a full executed counterexample, as opposed to a structural argument

rows.anchor: The symbol E has historically been overloaded. It has appeared as: Entity; Evidence in some tuples; endpoint of relationships; generic semantic object. ... the current graph model explicitly distinguishes 𝓔 for Entity from 𝓔_v for Evidence.
rows.statement: The symbol E is flagged as a recurring Ubiquitous-Language collision across the corpus, having denoted Entity, Evidence, a relationship endpoint, and a generic semantic object at different points; the current graph model already distinguishes calligraphic E (Entity) from E_v (Evidence).

rows.anchor: P=(x,d,v) where x∈𝓔, d∈𝓓, v∈V_d. 𝒫={(x,d,v) | x∈𝓔, d∈𝓓, v∈V_d}. This is mathematically cleaner than P=(E,D,V) because it avoids confusion between the type 𝓔 and an individual entity E.
rows.statement: Proposes renotating P=(E,D,V) as P=(x,d,v) with x in the Entity-type E, d in the Dimension-type D, v in V_d, and the proposition universe P={(x,d,v) | ...} — a purely notational refinement resolving the type-vs-instance and E-for-Entity/E-for-Evidence collisions, without changing the underlying (Entity,Dimension,Value) structure.

rows.anchor: Let x=Nexus, d=Version, v=3.69. Then P=(Nexus,Version,3.69). An assertion becomes A=(id,(Nexus,Version,3.69),e,c,t,Π). The same proposition can therefore occur in multiple assertions ... consistent with the already-proven distinction: Same proposition ≠ same assertion.
rows.statement: Worked example instantiating P=(Nexus,Version,3.69) inside a full Assertion, and observing that the identical proposition can recur across multiple distinct assertions A1,A2 (different id/evidence/context/temporal/provenance) — consistent with the already-established same-proposition-does-not-imply-same-assertion result.

rows.anchor: P1 =_str P2 ⟺ x1=x2 ∧ d1=d2 ∧ v1=v2. But semantic equality may be richer. For example 3.70m and 370cm may denote the same value. Thus P1 =_str P2 could be false while P1 ≡_sem P2 is true. Therefore the proposition type requires a value semantics, not merely a syntactic tuple.
rows.statement: Structural proposition equality is defined component-wise (x1=x2 and d1=d2 and v1=v2); a worked example (3.70m vs 370cm) shows structural equality can be false while semantic equality is true, because value semantics (unit conversion) are richer than syntactic tuple comparison — the proposition type therefore requires a value semantics, not merely structural comparison.

rows.anchor: v ∈ V_d requires a definition of V_d. For some dimensions V_d may be finite: Status={Unknown,Supported,Refuted}. For others V_d=ℝ. For others V_d=VersionStrings. For relationships V_d may itself be structured. Therefore P=(E,D,V) is not the end of the formalisation. It is the beginning of the typed
rows.statement: Resolving P=(x,d,v) exposes a deeper open subproblem: the value space V_d itself needs a definition per dimension, ranging over finite enumerations (e.g. Status), reals, version-string domains, or structured spaces for relational dimensions — P=(E,D,V) is the beginning of a typed semantic domain, not its end.

rows.anchor: D: 𝓔 → Type_D or equivalently V_D. Then v ∈ V_D. This gives the well-formedness rule: WF(P) ⟺ x∈𝓔 ∧ d∈𝓓 ∧ v∈V_d. This is a candidate invariant.
rows.statement: Dimension typing is formalized as a function from the entity universe (or equivalently a declared value space) to an admissible value type, yielding a candidate well-formedness invariant WF(P) iff x in E-universe and d in D-universe and v in V_d.

rows.anchor: Suppose P = "Alice manages Bob." ... some relationships are inherently n-ary: R(x1,x2,...,xn). The earlier corpus explicitly treats Relationship as a first-class knowledge construct and proposed r=(E1,E2,T,R,Q,E,Σ,τ). Therefore we must test whether P=(x,d,v) can represent all required relationships
rows.statement: A potential problem is raised for relational knowledge: while a binary relation like 'Alice manages Bob' can be squeezed into (x,d,v)=(Alice,Manager,Bob), some relationships are inherently n-ary, and the corpus has separately proposed an eight-field Relationship construct r=(E1,E2,T,R,Q,E,Sigma,tau); whether the simple (x,d,v) triple can represent all required relationships without distortion is left as an open sub-test, not resolved here.

rows.anchor: Model A — Relationship reducible to proposition: Relationship ⊆ Proposition. ... Model B — Relationship is a separate primitive: Relationship ⊄ Proposition. Then 𝒫 requires extension: 𝒫 = 𝒫_attribute ∪ 𝒫_relation. We must not choose between these merely by preference. It requires counterexamples.
rows.statement: Two competing, explicitly undecided models for relationships: Model A (Relationship is reducible to/a subset of Proposition, so P=(x,d,v) suffices) versus Model B (Relationship is a separate primitive, requiring the proposition universe to split into attribute-propositions and relation-propositions); the choice is explicitly deferred pending counterexamples rather than made by preference.

rows.anchor: Context c has already been shown to be necessary at assertion level ... the executed removal analysis explicitly reports context as irrecoverable. But that does not mean context should be inserted into P. ... Otherwise we risk destroying the distinction between proposition and assertion.
rows.statement: Context must not leak into the Proposition type: although context c is independently necessary at the Assertion level (an executed removal test found it irrecoverable), inserting it into P would collapse the proposition/assertion distinction — P remains the semantic proposition, c remains the situational assertion context.

rows.anchor: e is outside P. The executed removal test found that evidence cannot be derived from proposition content. Therefore P ≠ (P,e). Evidence is associated with the assertion, not intrinsic to proposition identity. This preserves Same(P) while allowing DifferentEvidence(A1,A2).
rows.statement: Evidence must not leak into the Proposition type: an executed removal test found evidence cannot be derived from proposition content, so P is not (P,e) — evidence attaches to the assertion, preserving that the same proposition can appear with different evidence across different assertions.

rows.anchor: t belongs to Assertion. The executed counterexample found that one proposition may have two validity intervals, forcing the system to wrap propositions in assertions. Therefore P must not carry assertion-specific validity ... Temporal multiplicity is an assertion phenomenon, not necessarily a propos
rows.statement: Major result: temporal validity t must not leak into P, because an executed counterexample found a single proposition can have two distinct validity intervals (requiring the system to wrap propositions in separate assertions to represent both) — temporal multiplicity is an assertion-level phenomenon, not a proposition-identity phenomenon.

rows.anchor: P1 ≡_P P2 iff x1 ≡_E x2, d1 ≡_D d2, and v1 ≡_{V_d} v2. This should remain a candidate formulation until value semantics are formally specified.
rows.statement: Candidate semantic proposition equality is defined component-wise via per-component equivalences (entity equivalence, dimension equivalence, and a domain-specific Normalize_D-based value equivalence, e.g. 3.70m equiv 370cm), explicitly held as a candidate pending formal value semantics.

rows.anchor: Proposition distinct from Assertion 🟢 Established ... Candidate P=(E,D,V) 🟢 Strongly supported ... Typed proposition 🟡 Candidate formalisation ... V_D formally defined 🔴 ... Relationship representation 🔴 ... Proposition canonicalization 🔴 ... P=(E,D,V) fully proven 🔴
rows.statement: Step 262's derivation-status table records: Proposition-distinct-from-Assertion and Entity/Dimension/Value each-necessary as established (green); the typed P=(x,d,v) formalisation and proposition semantic equality as yellow candidates; V_D's formal definition, relationship representation, n-ary/complex propositions, proposition canonicalization, and full proof of P=(E,D,V) all remain red/unresolved.

rows.anchor: Step 262 does not invalidate K=(A,R). Quite the opposite. It strengthens it. ... Knowledge State / Assertions / Assertion / id, Proposition P (Entity x, Dimension d, Value v), evidence reference e, context c, temporal validity t, provenance Π / Asserted Relations ℛ
rows.statement: Crucial finding: resolving P as (x,d,v) strengthens rather than reopens K=(A,R), yielding a clean hierarchy: Knowledge State -> Assertions A (each Assertion = id, Proposition P {Entity x, Dimension d, Value v}, evidence reference e, context c, temporal validity t, provenance Pi) -> and Asserted Relations R.

rows.anchor: G-A: P=(E,D,V) — what are E,D,V? ... candidate → typing → removal test → counterexample → closure → computability.
rows.statement: The remaining load-bearing gap is explicitly named G-A: what are Entity, Dimension and Value themselves (their internal definitions and typing), to be attacked with the same six-stage method used throughout this programme (candidate -> typing -> removal test -> counterexample -> closure -> computability), reconstructed from the historical corpus rather than freshly invented.

rows.anchor: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — LOAD-BEARING GAP NARROWED. ... Step 262 establishes the typed-triple proposition as the strongest current candidate and demonstrates why all three components are semantically necessary. It does not yet prove the complete proposition ontology. ... no user decision is currently re
rows.statement: Step 262 verdict: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — LOAD-BEARING GAP NARROWED; the typed triple P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) is the strongest current candidate proposition structure with all three components shown semantically necessary, but the complete proposition ontology (E, D, V_D domains, and relationship representation) is not yet proven; no user decision is currently required for K or Sigma; Step 263 is set up to attack Entity/Dimension/Value typing, asking whether they are genuinely primitive or derivable from a deeper structure.

rows.anchor: G-9 | E/V symbol collision | disambiguation | E=Entity/Events, V=Value/Vertices ... OPEN — terminology
rows.statement: Gap G-9 (not blocking, terminology only): the E (Entity/Events) and V (Value/Vertices) symbol collisions identified earlier in the programme remain open, with the resolution route being a rename in the canonical vocabulary.

rows.anchor: Step 263 is no longer an open discovery problem ... The non-step Q14 material already defines the three types, and the independent reconstruction explicitly classifies CB-2 as 'RESOLVED BY THE CORPUS — not by the verifier.' Therefore Step 263 should verify and formalize the existing type system, not
rows.statement: Methodological course-correction: Step 263 abandons its planned open-discovery framing on finding that Q14 already defines Entity/Dimension/Value and that a parallel independent reconstruction classifies gap CB-2 as resolved by the corpus itself rather than requiring verifier derivation; the step is redirected to verification/formalization of the existing corpus type system.

lineage_claims.target: Q14 / the independent reconstruction's CB-2 classification
lineage_claims.quote: the independent reconstruction explicitly classifies CB-2 as 'RESOLVED BY THE CORPUS — not by the verifier.'

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS corpus uses a broader semantic definition: Entity = subject of knowledge. Therefore we must not silently substitute DDDEntity for KnowledgeEntity. An event, relationship or concept may be a KnowledgeOS Entity under the current definition even though it would not necessarily be modele
rows.statement: DDD warning: KnowledgeOS's Entity (anything that can be the subject of knowledge — person, object, system, event, relationship, or concept) is deliberately broader than classical DDD's technical Entity notion (identity-continuity within a bounded context); the two must not be silently conflated, since an event, relationship, or concept can be a valid KnowledgeOS Entity without being modeled as a DDD Entity.

rows.anchor: Because Step 261 established identity as distinct from equality, we should not infer x∈𝓔 ⇒ x has one universal identity across all contexts. Instead: Entity is the semantic role, while EntityIdentity is a separate question.
rows.statement: Entity-as-semantic-role must be kept separate from EntityIdentity (which context-relative identity criteria apply to a given entity instance) — membership in the Entity type does not imply one universal cross-context identity, consistent with Step 261's identity/equality separation.

rows.anchor: d: Domain → V_d ... a dimension is not itself a value. It determines which values are admissible. ... d=(ID,Name,ValueSpace,Type,Domain). ... (Nexus,Version,3.69) can be well formed if 3.69∈V_Version. But (Nexus,Version,Blue) should fail if Blue∉V_Version.
rows.statement: Dimension is formalized functionally as a map from a domain of applicable entities to its value space (d: Domain -> V_d) and structurally as a 5-field record (ID, Name, ValueSpace, Type, Domain); this structure is what allows well-formedness to reject an out-of-value-space triple like (Nexus,Version,Blue).

rows.anchor: A database field version is an implementation representation. A KnowledgeOS Dimension is a semantic construct defining: meaning; domain; value space; type; comparison characteristics. Therefore DatabaseField ≠ KnowledgeDimension. The field may implement the dimension, but it does not define its sema
rows.statement: A KnowledgeOS Dimension is explicitly distinguished from a mere database field/column: the field may implement the dimension, but a Dimension additionally carries meaning, domain, value space, type, and comparison-characteristic semantics that the field alone does not define.

rows.anchor: Value(v)∈V_d ⟺ Dimension(v)=d ... A value is meaningful only relative to its dimension. For example: 3.69 by itself is semantically incomplete. But (Version,3.69) has meaning. ... v=(ID,Value,Dimension,Type). Therefore a Value is not simply an arbitrary scalar. It carries its dimensional semantics.
rows.statement: Value and Dimension are semantically inseparable: Value(v) is in V_d if and only if Dimension(v)=d, meaning a bare scalar like 3.69 is semantically incomplete without its dimension; the corpus's internal Value representation is a 4-field record (ID, Value, Dimension, Type), so a Value always carries its dimensional semantics rather than being an arbitrary scalar.

rows.anchor: | Candidate | Knowledge? | E ❌ | D ❌ | V ❌ | E+D ❌ | E+V ❌ | D+V ❌ | E+D+V ✅ | The earlier Knowledge Atom source explicitly records this conclusion.
rows.statement: A corpus-sourced minimality table (attributed to the earlier Knowledge Atom source) tests all seven non-empty subsets of {Entity,Dimension,Value} and finds every proper subset (E, D, V, E+D, E+V, D+V) insufficient to constitute knowledge, with only the full triple E+D+V succeeding.

lineage_claims.quote: The earlier Knowledge Atom source explicitly records this conclusion.

rows.anchor: The proposition triple is minimal for the knowledge-atom model. That does not automatically prove P=(E,D,V) is sufficient for every conceivable proposition ... The corpus itself contains competing forms P=(S,ρ,O,Γ) and P=(V_P,E_P), among others. The reconstruction correctly classifies these as compe
rows.statement: Explicit caveat on the minimality result: minimality within the knowledge-atom model does not prove P=(E,D,V) is universally sufficient — the corpus independently contains competing proposition forms P=(S,rho,O,Gamma) and P=(V_P,E_P) among others, which are retained as competing formulations rather than silently discarded; P=(E,D,V) is canonical within the established Q14 semantic model, not proven as the unique possible representation.

rows.anchor: P=(Bhīṣma,Relationship_To_Arjuna,Grandfather). The corpus explicitly treats this as valid. This creates a significant modeling question. ... Representation A — relationship as dimension/value ... Representation B — relationship as first-class object r=(E1,E2,T,R,Q,E,Σ,τ). ... Relationship may requir
rows.statement: Concrete relationship-representation counterexample: the corpus validly represents a relationship both as a dimension/value pair inside a proposition (P=(Bhishma,RelationshipToArjuna,Grandfather), 'Representation A') and as the separate first-class eight-field Relationship construct r=(E1,E2,T,R,Q,E,Sigma,tau) ('Representation B'), which can additionally carry relationship-specific evidence, epistemic status, validity, and qualifiers that the compact triple cannot; conclusion is that a relationship may need an Assertion-level wrapper even when its semantic core reduces to a proposition.

rows.anchor: P must not become P=(E,D,V,Σ,e,τ,Π) merely because those properties are important to an assertion. That would collapse two semantic levels. ... The canonical proposition explicitly has: no epistemic status; no evidence; no temporal validity; no provenance.
rows.statement: Restated invariant, now made an explicit constraint: the Proposition type must never absorb epistemic status, evidence, temporal validity, or provenance fields even though those matter at the Assertion level, since doing so would collapse the Proposition/Assertion semantic-level separation.

rows.anchor: Entity answers: What is being described? Dimension answers: Along which semantic axis is it being described? Value answers: What position does the entity occupy on that axis? ... roughly analogous to a typed subject–predicate–object structure, while remaining distinct from RDF or classical logical s
rows.statement: DDD-flavored interpretation assigning each component of P=(E,D,V) a distinct responsibility/question: Entity=subject ('what is being described'), Dimension=semantic predicate/axis ('along which axis'), Value=typed object of the predicate ('what position') — analogous to, but explicitly distinct from, RDF or classical subject-predicate-object logical syntax.

rows.anchor: 𝒫 ⊆ 𝓔×𝓓×𝒱 with the dependency V∈V_D. More precisely: 𝒫 = Σ_{E∈𝓔} Σ_{D∈𝓓} V_D. This is mathematically stronger than treating 𝓔×𝓓×𝒱 as an unrestricted Cartesian product. Because not every value is valid for every dimension.
rows.statement: Mathematical reformulation of the proposition space as a dependent sum (Sigma) type, P = Sum over E in Entity-universe of Sum over D in Dimension-universe of V_D, rather than an unrestricted Cartesian product E x D x V — a strictly stronger statement because it excludes value/dimension pairs where the value is not admissible for that dimension.

rows.anchor: D=SecurityStatus. Then V_D={Compliant,NonCompliant,Unknown}. So (Nexus,SecurityStatus,Compliant) is well formed. But (Nexus,SecurityStatus,3.69) is not. Thus WF(P)=false.
rows.statement: Worked example of the dependent-type well-formedness rule: for D=SecurityStatus with V_D={Compliant,NonCompliant,Unknown}, (Nexus,SecurityStatus,Compliant) is well-formed but (Nexus,SecurityStatus,3.69) is not, since 3.69 is not in V_SecurityStatus.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Proposition Space is typed. It is not: all triples. It is: all semantically valid triples. That allows validation to become a deterministic predicate: WF: 𝒫 → {true,false}.
rows.statement: Key mathematical significance stated: the KnowledgeOS proposition space is typed (the set of all semantically valid E-D-V triples, not all triples), which makes well-formedness checking a deterministic total predicate WF:P->{true,false} — described as a strong bridge between the conceptual theory and eventual implementation.

rows.anchor: Step 263 does not yet establish: all possible ValueSpaces are known; or all measurement-scale rules are complete; or all relationship forms reduce to (E,D,V); or semantic equality of values is decidable. Those are separate questions.
rows.statement: Explicit non-claims: Step 263 does not establish that all possible value spaces are known, that all measurement-scale rules are complete, that all relationship forms reduce to the (E,D,V) triple, or that semantic equality of values is decidable — each remains a separate open question.

rows.anchor: CB-2 = CLOSED BY THE CORPUS. This is an important correction to our previous trajectory. We should not continue treating P=(E,D,V) as an unresolved hypothesis. The corpus already establishes it, and the independent audit explicitly found it in Q14.
rows.statement: Step 263 verdict: gap CB-2 (what are E, D, V) is CLOSED BY THE CORPUS itself (via Q14), not by verifier derivation — P=(E,D,V) should no longer be treated as an unresolved hypothesis, though E, D, and V_D still require complete formal closure (value-space semantics, measurement scales, relationship representation, identity, normalization).

rows.anchor: STEP 264 — VALUE SPACE AND MEASUREMENT SEMANTICS ... establish, dimension by dimension: V_D and its allowable operations: Equality_D, Compatibility_D, Ordering_D, Distance_D, Aggregation_D. ... if D is nominal, v1≠v2 does not imply an ordering. If D is ordinal, v1<v2 may be meaningful, but v2−v1 nee
rows.statement: Sets up Step 264 to determine, per dimension, the value space V_D and its permitted operations (Equality_D, Compatibility_D, Ordering_D, Distance_D, Aggregation_D), governed by measurement-scale rules (nominal admits no ordering; ordinal admits ordering but not subtraction; interval admits subtraction but not ratios; ratio admits division), and flags an explicit open decision for version identifiers: whether their ordering should be lexical, semantic-version precedence, or some other rule, rather than ordinary real-number arithmetic.

rows.anchor: the measurement regime belongs to the Dimension, not to the numerical representation of an individual Value. ... What mathematical structure does V_D carry, and which operations on its values are actually legitimate? This is where the theory moves from a typed proposition to a typed measurement sema
rows.statement: Step 264 narrows Step 263's typed-proposition result to a measurement-semantics question: since the measurement regime belongs to the Dimension rather than to an individual Value's numeric representation, the task is to determine what mathematical structure V_D carries and which operations on it are legitimate.

rows.anchor: RepresentationType(D) and ScaleType(D). For Version: RepresentationType=String/StructuredVersion while ScaleType=Ordinal is the proposed semantic interpretation. ... Type(D) cannot be reduced to programming-language type.
rows.statement: A dimension's RepresentationType (its storage/syntactic form, e.g. String/StructuredVersion for Version) is distinguished from its ScaleType (its measurement semantics, e.g. proposed Ordinal for Version) — a dimension's semantic Type cannot be reduced to a programming-language type.

rows.anchor: WF(P) ⟺ E∈𝓔 ∧ D∈𝓓 ∧ V∈V_D ∧ SemanticValid_D(V). The first three conjuncts are corpus-established. The final formulation is a derived refinement, not yet a corpus theorem.
rows.statement: Well-formedness is refined to add a fourth conjunct, SemanticValid_D(V) (the value belongs to the dimension's declared semantic value space, not merely something the programming language accepts), explicitly flagged as a derived refinement rather than an already-proven corpus theorem.

rows.anchor: Q14 explicitly says Version→Interval. But the later audit contests this classification ... If Version is Interval, then the formal system licenses 3.69-3.68=0.01 as a meaningful difference. ... version ordering can disagree with naïve decimal ordering. For example, semantic versions such as 3.10 and
rows.statement: The 'most important adversarial test' of the step: Q14's classification of Version as Interval would license a meaningless difference (3.69-3.68=0.01) and conflicts with the fact that semantic-version ordering (3.10 succeeds 3.9) disagrees with naive decimal ordering — Version must not be treated as an ordinary real number.

lineage_claims.quote: Q14 explicitly says Version→Interval. But the later audit contests this classification

rows.anchor: Version = StructuredOrdinal as the strongest candidate. ... 3.9<3.10 may be meaningful under semantic-version precedence, while 3.10-3.9 is not. ... StructuredOrdinal Version = Verifier Recommendation, not a corpus-established correction. The source corpus itself still contains the Interval classifi
rows.statement: Recommended resolution of the Version-scale dispute: Version=StructuredOrdinal (ordering meaningful under semantic-version precedence, but differences not), explicitly classified as a verifier recommendation, not yet a corpus-established correction, since the corpus's own Q14 material still classifies Version as Interval.

rows.anchor: D=(id,name,domain,V_D,σ) where σ is the measurement/scale structure. ... σ∈{Nominal,Ordinal,Interval,Ratio,…}. This does not mean σ is an additional component of the proposition. It remains metadata/structure of the Dimension.
rows.statement: Dimension is refined to a five-field candidate object D=(id,name,domain,V_D,sigma), where sigma is the measurement/scale-structure tag (Nominal/Ordinal/Interval/Ratio/...); sigma is explicitly Dimension metadata, not an additional field of the Proposition triple.

rows.anchor: V_D is not merely a set of allowed literals. It is a typed semantic space carrying a measurement regime. Therefore D = (domain, value space, semantic type, measurement regime) is the more mathematically meaningful interpretation of the existing Dimension construct.
rows.statement: What Step 264 closes: V_D is reconceived as a typed semantic space carrying a measurement regime rather than a bare set of allowed literals, giving Dimension the more mathematically meaningful shape D=(domain, value space, semantic type, measurement regime).

rows.anchor: STEP 265 — PROPOSITION IDENTITY AND SEMANTIC EQUALITY. The central question will be: P1=P2? More precisely: (E1,D1,V1) ≡ (E2,D2,V2) under: entity identity; dimension identity; value normalization; admissible transformations; context independence.
rows.statement: Sets up Step 265 to determine full proposition identity/semantic equality (E1,D1,V1) equiv (E2,D2,V2), requiring entity identity, dimension identity, value normalization, admissible transformations, and context independence to all be resolved together.

rows.anchor: Is Policy part of P (the proposition)? NO. Q14 §5.3 states a proposition 'has no epistemic status, has no evidence, has no temporal validity, has no provenance.' A policy is none of a proposition's three components (Entity, Dimension, Value). Counterexample: (Nexus, Version, 3.69) is the same propos
rows.statement: Policy is proven NOT part of the Proposition P=(Entity,Dimension,Value): the concrete proposition (Nexus,Version,3.69) is identical under every policy, and Q14 §5.3 already excludes epistemic status/evidence/temporal validity/provenance from Proposition, none of which Policy is either.

rows.anchor: Policy undefined -> CLOSED — corpus 57.47 + 42.9, executed ... Assessment uncomputable -> CLOSED — Policy supplies the missing parameter ... Σ underdetermined -> CLOSED — (dir,str) + Γ, PF-6 dissolved ... Assurance contradictory -> CLOSED — split four ways ... P = (E,D,V) undefined -> CLOSED — Q14
rows.statement: Five previously open gaps are confirmed CLOSED as of this mandate: Policy undefined (closed via 57.47+42.9, executed), Assessment uncomputable (closed once Policy supplies the missing parameter), Sigma underdetermined (closed via (dir,str)+Gamma, PF-6 dissolved), Assurance contradictory (closed via the four-way split), and P=(E,D,V) undefined (closed via Q14).

rows.anchor: Entity membership = UNDER-SPECIFIED unless an explicit ontology/registration boundary is introduced. ... Entity definition is conceptually clear but Entity membership is not universally decidable. ... Dimension: StructuralValidDimension(D) is computable ... but Structural validity ≠ Semantic adequac
rows.statement: Per-object computability audit for Entity, Dimension, Value and Proposition: Entity's semantic definition ('subject of knowledge') is conceptually clear but membership is not universally decidable without an explicit ontology/registration boundary; Dimension's structural validity is computable but semantic adequacy is not; Value membership is computable only where its value space V_D has an effective representation, ranging from trivially decidable (finite sets) through grammar-parseable (formal version strings) to fundamentally undecidable (open-ended conceptual domains); Proposition well-formedness is therefore CONDITIONALLY COMPUTABLE, contingent on all three membership predicates being computable.

rows.anchor: Every derived object bottoms out at layer 0, and layer 0 is finite and enumerable ... That is what makes WellFormed, StructuralValid, membership and equality all decidable — they reduce to finite set membership. The single most consequential structural fact: V ∈ V_D is decidable because V_D is decla
rows.statement: Explains why the whole theory is computable at all: every derived object bottoms out at the finite, enumerable Layer 0 primitives, which is what makes WellFormed, StructuralValid, membership and equality reduce to decidable finite-set membership; the single most consequential structural fact in the entire theory is that V in V_D is decidable specifically because Q14 attached ValueSpace to Dimension — without that single design decision, WellFormed(P) would be undecidable and T would have no structural guard at all.

lexical.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)

formal.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.

operational.anchor: I ran the experiment as a small executable epistemic model, using the 10 evidence cases we defined.

governance.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.

rationale_evidence.anchor: LogicalValidity \neq EmpiricalTruth
rationale_evidence.statement: States Conclusion≠Truth as fundamental: even Γ⊨P only means P follows from Γ under the specified formal system, not that the premises describe reality correctly, giving LogicalValidity≠EmpiricalTruth — 'one of the most important mathematical safeguards in the architecture'. Worked compliance example distinguishes Proposition A (Nexus.version=3.69, a factual claim supported by runtime/DB/LLM evidence E_1,E_2,E_3) from Proposition B (does production Nexus satisfy the required version), where an architecture document stating 'required>=3.85' is used as a NORMATIVE CONSTRAINT combined with runtime evidence (3.69), NOT as evidence that Nexus actually runs 3.85 — 'the architecture document was not evidence that Nexus was 3.85; it was a normative constraint used together with runtime evidence'. This yields EpistemicCorrectness ≠ DomainAdequacy: KnowledgeOS can know something accurately (well-supported Nexus.version=3.69) while that thing is undesirable (violates the >=3.85 requirement) — the discrepancy is 'the current state is well-supported but does not satisfy the ideal constraint', not 'evidence says Nexus is wrong'.

rationale_evidence.anchor: I have read DeepSeek's proposed **Computational Closure 3 — Evidence**.
rationale_evidence.statement: Explicit corpus provenance detail: one section is attributed by name to 'DeepSeek' proposing its own Computational Closure 3 - Evidence (E=(P,S,R,T,Q,Π,C), relation types Supports/Contradicts/Contextualizes/Qualifies, quality tuple Q=(Reliability,Relevance,Currency,Independence,Completeness)), which is then reviewed by a distinct 'senior mathematician and DDD architect' voice — direct evidence that this strand of the corpus involved cross-model critique and revision cycles (at least two different AI systems contributing competing formalizations of the same closure).

rationale_evidence.anchor: A(\{e\}) \approx A(\{e,e\})
rationale_evidence.statement: Law E4 Duplicate Idempotence: adding an exact duplicate of existing evidence must not create additional independent evidential support, A({e})≈A({e,e}) — otherwise 'an attacker could simply submit the same observation 1000 times and manufacture confidence'. Law E5 distinguishes this from genuine corroboration: IndependentCorroboration ≠ DuplicateEvidence — two genuinely independent sources supporting P (e.g. a database and a separate monitoring system) SHOULD generally increase support relative to either alone, provided the policy recognizes both as relevant and reliable.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Q14 §3.4 classifies value-space types as Nominal / Ordinal / Interval / Ratio ... But Q14 gives version numbers as its example of an INTERVAL scale. That is wrong ... Version is ORDINAL at best.
rationale_evidence.statement: Measurement-theory correction contesting the corpus: question-14 correctly attaches Nominal/Ordinal/Interval/Ratio scale typing to the Dimension (not the Value), but wrongly classifies version numbers as Interval — 3.69-3.68 has no meaningful unit-magnitude, version ordering is not numeric ordering (3.10 > 3.9 as versions but 3.10 < 3.9 as decimals), and Interval requires equal intervals to mean equal differences, which versions lack; version scale is Ordinal at best, and since Nexus.Version is the corpus's most-used worked example, an inadmissible-arithmetic hazard sits inside the canonical illustration — explicit VERIFIER RECOMMENDATION contesting the corpus.
