sources.note: A same-day formal-specification reading of the v1.0 Definitions/Axioms/Theorems document treating it as source material to DERIVE further theory from, rather than add new external concepts to: identifies and repairs one fundamental inconsistency in v1.0 (the epistemic state E_{a,c,t} was allowed to contain non-factive attitudes like false hypotheses while simultaneously being called 'knowledge', contradicting the factivity axiom), repairing it via KnowledgeAttribution(K_t) subset-of EpistemicState(K_t) and a three-level chain EpistemicState -> Determination -> KnowledgeAttribution; derives a candidate epistemic-state type K_t=(E_t,rho_t,alpha_t,pi_t,tau_t); derives a semantic (non-syntactic) atomicity criterion Atomic(k) iff SemanticallyIndivisible(k); derives a Hypothesis Space H_Q from Inquiry and makes Determination set-valued Det(E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)=A_t subset-of H_Q; derives Sat/Req/Delta/Zero/Adequate identical in spirit to the companion Gap-theory document; derives a four-way Unknown taxonomy (Unobserved/Uninterpreted/Underdetermined/Unobservable); re-derives Lord/Sarathi/Decision/Authorization as four cleanly separated DDD responsibilities (candidate generation / epistemic navigation / selection / institutional legitimacy); derives a non-circular behavioral definition of semantic equivalence Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R1)= Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R2) for all (Q,C,EC); re-derives Identity independently of state equality via a persistent identifier; produces ten Derived Propositions P1-P10; reduces the prior seven open questions to five remaining research problems R1-R5 (truth semantics, semantic equivalence proof obligations, transition algebra, knowledge attribution function Gamma, kernel minimality); corrects v1.0's self-description from 'complete theory' to 'semantically closed, formally not yet proved complete'; and announces the next document 'KnowledgeOS Theory v1.1 -- Formal Derivation from Definitions' with four named theorems to prove first (Epistemic State Theorem, Adequacy/Gap/Zero Theorem, Evidence Assessment Theorem, Semantic Preservation Theorem). Possibly a continuation chapter of the same v1.0 milestone, possibly its own v1.1 artifact -- not resolved within this batch.

rows.anchor: But it also defines the epistemic state as potentially containing: beliefs, hypotheses, commitments, questions, rejections, knowledge, uncertainty, alternatives. Therefore: E_{a,c,t} != Knowledge and more specifically: Knowledge subseteq EpistemicState ... If E_t contains false hypotheses, how can E_t itself be called "knowledge"?
rows.statement: Identifies one fundamental inconsistency in v1.0: the epistemic state E_{a,c,t} is defined as potentially containing non-factive attitudes (beliefs, hypotheses, rejections, uncertainty) while Knowledge is separately defined as factive, producing a contradiction if E_t is also called 'knowledge' -- since if E_t contains false hypotheses it cannot itself be knowledge; repairs this by establishing Knowledge as a proper semantic subset of EpistemicState (Knowledge subseteq EpistemicState), not identical to it.

rows.anchor: $$E_{a,c,t}=\text{Epistemic State}$$ and: $$K_{a,c,t}=KnowledgeAttribution(E_{a,c,t})$$ where: K_{a,c,t} subseteq E_{a,c,t}. This is a **derived consequence**, not a new philosophical assumption. ... EpistemicState -> Determination -> KnowledgeAttribution.
rows.statement: Derives the corrected three-level chain: Level 1 EpistemicState E_{a,c,t} (everything the participant currently holds), Level 2 Determination Det(E_{a,c,t},Q,C,S) (what current evidence and standards warrant), Level 3 KnowledgeAttribution Knows(a,p,c,t) (what qualifies as knowledge), with K_{a,c,t}=KnowledgeAttribution(E_{a,c,t}) subset-of E_{a,c,t} -- explicitly a DERIVED consequence of the existing definitions, not a new philosophical assumption.

rows.anchor: $$\mathcal{KS}=\operatorname{SemDomain}(\mathcal C)$$ and: KS need not itself be a metric, probability or measure space. ... We do **not** need to search for: graph vs lattice vs category vs metric space as competing ontologies. ... particular mathematical structures are **models/projections of C**.
rows.statement: Derives that Knowledge Space KS=SemDomain(C) need not itself be metric/probability/measure space, dissolving the earlier competing-ontology search (graph vs lattice vs category vs metric space) since any particular mathematical structure is merely a model/projection of the already-defined many-sorted core C.

rows.anchor: $$K_t=(E_t,\rho_t,\alpha_t,\pi_t,\tau_t)$$ where E_t=epistemic content/state, rho_t=semantic relations, alpha_t=epistemic attributions/assessments, pi_t=provenance structure, tau_t=temporal validity/history references. ... K_t in EpiState ... K = {well-formed epistemic states over C}. ... the first serious candidate for closing OPEN-1/OPEN-2.
rows.statement: Proposes a five-component candidate type for K_t=(E_t,rho_t,alpha_t,pi_t,tau_t) (content, semantic relations, attributions/assessments, provenance, temporal validity), abstracted further as K_t in the class EpiState of well-formed epistemic structures over the core C, giving K = {well-formed epistemic states over C} -- explicitly offered as the first serious candidate closing the still-open K_t-type question.
missing: a precise definition of 'well-formed' for EpiState

rows.anchor: An epistemic object is not necessarily atomic. ... k_i="minimal semantically closed substructure" if such a minimal substructure exists. ... Atomic(k) iff: 1. k denotes a coherent semantic commitment; 2. removing any required component destroys its semantic identity; 3. splitting it produces components that no longer independently preserve the original commitment. ... Atomic(k) iff SemanticallyIndivisible(k).
rows.statement: Derives a semantic (non-syntactic) atomicity criterion: a knowledge atom k_i is redefined as a minimal semantically closed substructure rather than a flat tuple, with Atomic(k) formally iff k denotes a coherent semantic commitment, removing any required component destroys its semantic identity, and splitting it yields components that no longer independently preserve the original commitment -- Atomic(k) iff SemanticallyIndivisible(k), a testable definition of atomicity rather than an arbitrary field-count.
missing: an operational test procedure for SemanticallyIndivisible

rows.anchor: $$EA(e,h,\mathcal H,M,S,C)$$ ... EA:ExHxHxMxSxC -> A ... This does **not** make KnowledgeOS Bayesian. A Bayesian likelihood ratio is simply one possible implementation ... A logical regime could instead produce: Entails, Contradicts, Undetermined. ... EvidenceAssessment is core-semantic; its mathematical realization is regime-specific.
rows.statement: Integrates Good's evidence-assessment concept cleanly into the regime architecture: EA(e,h,H,M,S,C) -> A is a core-semantic function whose mathematical REALIZATION is regime-specific (a Bayesian likelihood ratio in a probabilistic regime, Entails/Contradicts/Undetermined in a logical regime, Observed/ErrorBound/CalibrationStatus in a measurement regime) -- EvidenceAssessment is core-semantic, its realization regime-specific, so this does not make KnowledgeOS Bayesian.

rows.anchor: $$\mathcal H_Q=\{h\mid h\text{ is an admissible candidate interpretation/explanation for }Q\}.$$ ... Reject(h1) not=> Accept(h2). ... Determine(Q) -> A_Q where A_Q subseteq H_Q is the set of candidates still epistemically admissible.
rows.statement: Derives the missing Hypothesis Space H_Q from Inquiry Q=(Target,Purpose,Context,Requirements) as the set of admissible candidate interpretations/explanations for Q, reinforcing Reject(h1) does not imply Accept(h2), and redefining Determine(Q) not as 'choose one candidate' but as producing A_Q subset-of H_Q, the set of candidates still epistemically admissible.

rows.anchor: $$Det(E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)=\mathcal A_t$$ where A_t={h in H_Q: Warrant(h|E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)}. Unique determination |A_t|=1. Multiple admissible interpretations |A_t|>1. No admissible hypothesis |A_t|=0. This is much more general than a simple TRUE/FALSE.
rows.statement: Redefines Determination as a set-valued operation Det(E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)=A_t={h in H_Q: Warrant(h|E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)}, admitting three distinguishable outcomes -- unique determination |A_t|=1, multiple admissible interpretations |A_t|>1, and no admissible hypothesis |A_t|=0 -- strictly more general than a binary TRUE/FALSE status.

rows.anchor: Determined != Known. A proposition can be determined under an operational standard without us being entitled to assert semantic factivity. ... Determined_S(p) and: Knows(a,p,c,t). ... Warrant != Truth. and: Determination != Factivity.
rows.statement: Derives Determined != Known: a proposition can be operationally determined (Determined_S(p)) without licensing the factive Knows(a,p,c,t) relation, since a statistical model can produce a highly warranted conclusion while its assumptions are wrong -- giving Warrant != Truth and Determination != Factivity.

rows.anchor: $$Adeq(K,Q,C,EC)\iff \forall r\in Req(Q,C,EC),\ Sat(K,r).$$ This is a genuine derivation from the definitions. ... $$\Delta(K,Q,C,EC)=\{r\in Req(Q,C,EC):\neg Sat(K,r)\}.$$ ... Zero(K,Q,C,EC) iff Delta(K,Q,C,EC)=empty. ... Zero is not a number. It is a **predicate over an empty requirement residual**.
rows.statement: Derives Adeq(K,Q,C,EC) iff for all r in Req(Q,C,EC), Sat(K,r) -- a genuine derivation from existing definitions rather than a new assumption -- and correspondingly Delta(K,Q,C,EC)={r in Req: not Sat(K,r)} with Zero iff Delta=empty, stronger than the prior K models EC formulation since it identifies exactly what the discrepancy is; states Zero is not a number but a predicate over an empty requirement residual (independently converging with the companion Gap-theory document's identical formalization).

rows.anchor: Gap is therefore not distance. ... Delta_t is first a **residual requirement structure**. Only afterwards may a regime define: d(Delta_t) or: Severity(Delta_t). Thus: Gap -> Requirement Residual -> optional Measurement. This eliminates the temptation to invent a universal Knowledge Distance.
rows.statement: States Gap -> Requirement Residual -> optional Measurement as the correct hierarchy, eliminating the temptation to invent a universal Knowledge Distance -- independently convergent with the companion Gap-theory document's semantic-before-numerical discipline.

rows.anchor: U1 -- Unobserved: Obs(r)=empty. U2 -- Uninterpreted: Obs(r)!=empty, Interpret(r)=empty. U3 -- Underdetermined: |A_r|>1. U4 -- Unobservable: Observable(r)=False. Therefore: Unknown != Unobserved != Uninterpreted != Underdetermined != Unobservable.
rows.statement: Derives a four-kind Unknown taxonomy for a requirement r: U1 Unobserved (no relevant observation exists, Obs(r)=empty); U2 Uninterpreted (observation exists but no valid semantic interpretation, Interpret(r)=empty); U3 Underdetermined (evidence exists but does not sufficiently distinguish admissible hypotheses, |A_r|>1); U4 Unobservable (the property cannot be established through any available channel, Observable(r)=False) -- giving a five-way non-collapse and a major refinement of Zero.

rows.anchor: Lord does not need to "invent unknown unknowns." Instead: Lord(K_t,Delta_t,Q_t) -> CandidateSet_t ... Candidate != Knowledge. So Lord becomes a **candidate-generation mechanism**, not a truth mechanism. ... Guide:(K_t,Delta_t,A_t^act,Q_t,C_t)->Preference_t. Then: Preference_t != Decision. And: Decision != Authorization. ... Lord=candidate generation, Sarathi=epistemic navigation, Decision=selection, Authorization=institutional legitimacy.
rows.statement: Re-derives Lord (Lord(K_t,Delta_t,Q_t) -> CandidateSet_t, a candidate-generation mechanism, not a truth mechanism, since Candidate != Knowledge) and Sarathi (Guide(K_t,Delta_t,A_t^act,Q_t,C_t)->Preference_t, with Preference_t != Decision and Decision != Authorization) into a cleanly separated four-role DDD chain: Lord=candidate generation, Sarathi=epistemic navigation, Decision=selection, Authorization=institutional legitimacy.

rows.anchor: $$K_{t+1}=\Theta(K_t,e_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,S_t,M_t,\mathcal H_t,EC_t)$$ ... The transition is valid only if: WellFormed(K_{t+1}) AND Invariant(K_t,K_{t+1}) and provenance records the transition.
rows.statement: Derives the full transition semantics K_{t+1}=Theta(K_t,e_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,S_t,M_t,H_t,EC_t), valid only if the resulting state is well-formed AND preserves declared invariants relative to K_t, with the transition itself recorded in provenance.

rows.anchor: History = **transition provenance** rather than simply "old versions." ... K_t is a snapshot, while H_{<=t} is the trajectory. Hence: CurrentState != History.
rows.statement: Derives History as transition provenance (H={(E_t,theta_t,E_{t+1})}) rather than simply 'old versions', with K_t as a snapshot and H_{<=t} as the full trajectory, giving CurrentState != History.

rows.anchor: $$Identity(x_t,x_{t+1})\iff PersistentIdentifier(x_t)=PersistentIdentifier(x_{t+1})$$ provided the identity contract permits continuity. ... SameIdentity not=> SameState. and: DifferentState not=> DifferentIdentity. This directly addresses the earlier unresolved example of Nexus RAM changing from 31 GB to 32 GB.
rows.statement: Derives Identity independently of state equality via a persistent-identifier carrier iota(x): Identity(x_t,x_{t+1}) iff PersistentIdentifier(x_t)=PersistentIdentifier(x_{t+1}) (subject to the identity contract permitting continuity), giving SameIdentity does not imply SameState and DifferentState does not imply DifferentIdentity -- directly resolving the earlier open Nexus-RAM-changed example.

rows.anchor: Let Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R) be the externally observable epistemic behavior of representation R. Then: $$R_1\equiv_{sem}R_2 \iff \forall (Q,C,EC)\in\mathcal D: Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R_1)=Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R_2).$$ The observable behavior must include at least: {Identity,Meaning,EvidenceRelations,Assessment,Gap,Determination,History,ValidTransitions}. This removes the circularity
rows.statement: Derives a non-circular definition of semantic equivalence: R1 =_sem R2 iff Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R1)=Obs_{EC,Q,C}(R2) for all (Q,C,EC) in the admissible domain, where the observable behaviour must include at least eight named aspects (Identity, Meaning, EvidenceRelations, Assessment, Gap, Determination, History, ValidTransitions) -- explicitly removing the circularity of defining equivalence via 'they mean the same thing', reframing semantic equivalence as behavioral equivalence under declared epistemic contexts.
missing: proof that this relation is reflexive, symmetric, transitive, representation-independent and sufficiently discriminating (named R2 below)

rows.anchor: $$K_{min}=\operatorname{argmin}_{R\in\mathcal R}Complexity(R)$$ subject to: SemanticAdequacy AND TransitionCompleteness AND InvariantPreservation. This is exactly why the old 8 vs 13 experiment could not determine the kernel. ... what must be held constant: semantic carrier + capability contract + observable behavior before comparing minimal representations.
rows.statement: Redefines kernel minimality as K_min = argmin over admissible representations R of Complexity(R), subject to SemanticAdequacy, TransitionCompleteness, and InvariantPreservation simultaneously, explaining why the 8-vs-13 experiment could not determine a kernel: what must be held constant before comparing minimal representations is the semantic carrier, the capability contract, and observable behaviour together -- none of which were fixed in that experiment.

rows.anchor: $$Regime=(Projection,Structure,Semantics,Inference,Measurement,Assumptions).$$ And therefore every result has the form: $$Result_R=Inference_R(F_R(\pi_R(\mathcal C))).$$ Hence: Result_R != Knowledge unless the knowledge attribution rules independently license that conclusion. This is the **anti-contamination principle**.
rows.statement: Derives the general regime-result equation Result_R = Inference_R(F_R(pi_R(C))), giving the anti-contamination principle Result_R != Knowledge unless the knowledge-attribution rules independently license that conclusion -- a formal restatement of the anti-corruption principle now expressed as a derivation rather than a bare axiom.

rows.anchor: Good's evidence weight can be represented as: $$W_R(e;h_i,h_j)$$ inside a probabilistic/statistical regime. But KnowledgeOS retains: Evidence -> Assessment -> Determination -> KnowledgeAttribution. Thus: Good enriches EvidenceAssessment; Good does not redefine Knowledge.
rows.statement: Places Good's Weight-of-Evidence apparatus precisely within the architecture: W_R(e;hi,hj) is one regime-specific realization inside a probabilistic/statistical regime, while KnowledgeOS retains its own Evidence->Assessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution chain -- 'Good enriches EvidenceAssessment; Good does not redefine Knowledge', named the correct integration.

rows.anchor: P1 State/Knowledge separation: KnowledgeAttribution(K_t) subseteq EpistemicState(K_t). P2 Requirement-residual gap. P3 Zero criterion. P4 Determination is potentially set-valued. P5 Rejection does not imply truth. P6 Evidence assessment is target-relative. P7 State evolution is non-monotonic. P8 State equality is not identity. P9 Representation equivalence precedes minimality. P10 Mathematical regime non-contamination.
rows.statement: Consolidates ten Derived Propositions (P1-P10) as the file's formal upgrade to the theory: P1 KnowledgeAttribution(K_t) subset EpistemicState(K_t); P2 Delta_t={r in Req_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}; P3 Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty; P4 Det(Q,K_t) subset H_Q; P5 h1 not-in Det does not imply h2 in Det; P6 EA=EA(E,H,H_space,M,S,C); P7 K_t not-subset K_{t+1} in general; P8 K_t!=K_{t+1} does not imply identity loss; P9 R1=_sem R2 must be established before comparing complexity; P10 Result_R not-equiv Knowledge without an independent attribution step.

rows.anchor: K_t type: Strong candidate derived. Semantic equivalence: Formal candidate derived. Atomic unit: Atomicity criterion derived. Gap structure: Requirement-residual derivation available. Adequacy: Can be defined from satisfaction. Transition semantics: Framework derived; transition laws remain. Kernel minimality: Still genuinely open. That is a substantial reduction.
rows.statement: Re-assesses the prior seven open questions against the new derivations: K_t type, semantic equivalence, and atomic unit each now have a strong/formal candidate derived; gap structure and adequacy can now be fully defined from satisfaction; transition semantics has a derived framework with laws still needed; kernel minimality remains genuinely open -- a substantial reduction in open-question severity.

rows.anchor: R1 -- Truth semantics: KnowledgeOS cannot derive objective truth merely from evidence. This is deliberately external to the system unless a domain provides a truth oracle. R2 -- Semantic equivalence: we still need to prove that it is reflexive, symmetric, transitive, representation-independent, sufficiently discriminating. R3 -- Transition algebra: laws for revision, supersession, contradiction, reinstatement, merge, split, temporal invalidation. R4 -- Knowledge attribution: Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)->KnowledgeAttributions, probably the most important remaining epistemological problem. R5 -- Kernel minimality: only after R1-R4 are sufficiently specified.
rows.statement: Reduces the entire remaining research problem to five fundamental problems R1-R5: R1 Truth semantics (True(p,c,t) is deliberately external to KnowledgeOS absent a domain truth oracle); R2 Semantic equivalence (a candidate behavioral definition exists but reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity/representation-independence/sufficient-discrimination remain proof obligations); R3 Transition algebra (laws for revision/supersession/contradiction/reinstatement/merge/split/temporal invalidation still needed); R4 Knowledge attribution function Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t)->KnowledgeAttributions, named probably the most important remaining epistemological problem; R5 Kernel minimality, solvable only after R1-R4.

rows.anchor: **KnowledgeOS Theory v1.0 is a semantically closed conceptual theory and a partially formalized mathematical theory.** ... Calling those "solved" would be scientifically too strong. ... Current status: **KnowledgeOS Theory v1.0 — SEMANTICALLY CLOSED** but: **FORMALLY NOT YET PROVED COMPLETE**
rows.statement: Corrects v1.0's own self-description from 'complete KnowledgeOS theory at the theory/architecture level' to the more precise 'semantically closed conceptual theory and a partially formalized mathematical theory', formally classifying current status as SEMANTICALLY CLOSED but FORMALLY NOT YET PROVED COMPLETE, since Truth, SemanticEquivalence, Attribution, TransitionCompleteness and KernelMinimality remain unproven.

rows.anchor: What is the mathematical structure of Knowledge? ... a better question: **What mathematical structure must preserve the semantics of an epistemic state?** ... SemanticRequirements -> Structure -> MathematicalRepresentation rather than: Mathematics -> Knowledge.
rows.statement: Names the file's deepest reframing as the 'really important breakthrough': replacing the question 'what is the mathematical structure of Knowledge' with 'what mathematical structure must preserve the semantics of an epistemic state', giving the direction SemanticRequirements -> Structure -> MathematicalRepresentation rather than Mathematics -> Knowledge.

rows.anchor: **KnowledgeOS Theory v1.1 — Formal Derivation from Definitions** with this order: Definitions -> Derived Propositions -> Lemmas -> Theorems -> Counterexamples -> Proof Obligations -> Kernel Minimality. ... 1. Epistemic State Theorem ... 2. Adequacy/Gap/Zero Theorem ... 3. Evidence Assessment Theorem ... 4. Semantic Preservation Theorem ... Only after those four are stable should we touch the 8/13 kernel question again.
rows.statement: Announces the next planned document 'KnowledgeOS Theory v1.1 -- Formal Derivation from Definitions' with a seven-stage internal order (Definitions -> Derived Propositions -> Lemmas -> Theorems -> Counterexamples -> Proof Obligations -> Kernel Minimality) and four specific first theorems to prove (Epistemic State Theorem characterizing E; Adequacy/Gap/Zero Theorem deriving Sat/Delta/Zero; Evidence Assessment Theorem deriving hypothesis-relative assessment without assuming Bayesianism; Semantic Preservation Theorem establishing the equivalence relation needed before kernel minimality) -- explicitly gating the 8/13 kernel question behind these four.

sources.note: Step 266's full computability audit of every principal KnowledgeOS object/operation, deriving a three-layer (deterministic core / external parametric semantics / normative assessment boundary) architecture and a candidate Computability Boundary Principle; concludes computability is partially established, not closed, and that the real requirement is making the computation/judgment boundary visible rather than eliminating judgment.

rows.anchor: Computable ≠ Implementable in principle but Computable = effective, typed, terminating procedure with defined semantics. It also explicitly forbids calling something computable merely because a program could approximate it.
rows.statement: Precise computability criterion: a predicate/function/relation/operation is computable only if it is an effective, typed, terminating procedure with defined semantics (defined inputs/types, termination, deterministic result; for transformations, also a defined domain and codomain) — explicitly distinct from and stronger than mere in-principle implementability.

rows.anchor: Class A — directly computable ... Class B — computable only after semantic parameters are supplied ... Class C — not computable as currently defined ... Authoritative(x) Relevant(x) Correct(x) Adequate(x) when no operational decision procedure or authoritative source is defined.
rows.statement: The theory's predicates/operations are sorted into three computability classes: Class A directly computable (structural parsing, identifier lookup, hashing, canonical serialization, deterministic transformation on fixed inputs), Class B computable only once semantic parameters are supplied (ValidOperation(D,o) needs a scale/type registry; Resolve(pi) needs a provenance registry), and Class C not computable as currently defined (Authoritative(x), Relevant(x), Correct(x), Adequate(x) — predicates with no operational decision procedure, exposing hidden human judgment).

rows.anchor: Entity membership = UNDER-SPECIFIED unless an explicit ontology/registration boundary is introduced. ... Entity definition is conceptually clear but Entity membership is not universally decidable. ... Dimension: StructuralValidDimension(D) is computable ... but Structural validity ≠ Semantic adequac
rows.statement: Per-object computability audit for Entity, Dimension, Value and Proposition: Entity's semantic definition ('subject of knowledge') is conceptually clear but membership is not universally decidable without an explicit ontology/registration boundary; Dimension's structural validity is computable but semantic adequacy is not; Value membership is computable only where its value space V_D has an effective representation, ranging from trivially decidable (finite sets) through grammar-parseable (formal version strings) to fundamentally undecidable (open-ended conceptual domains); Proposition well-formedness is therefore CONDITIONALLY COMPUTABLE, contingent on all three membership predicates being computable.

rows.anchor: StructuralValidation(A) can be computable, while Truth(A) cannot be assumed computable. ... Finite Status Algebra ⇒ Computable transition validation. But that does not make the assignment of the status computable. ... TransitionValidity ≠ StatusAssignment. This is one of the most important hidden bo
rows.statement: Two of the audit's sharpest distinctions: (1) an Assertion's structural validation is computable while its Truth is not assumed computable; (2) given a finite epistemic-status algebra, mechanically validating whether a status TRANSITION is legal is computable, but this does NOT make the ASSIGNMENT of a status to an assertion (whether evidence actually warrants that status) computable — TransitionValidity != StatusAssignment is named one of the most important hidden boundaries in the whole theory.

rows.anchor: StructuralEquality = COMPUTABLE under canonical representation. ... SemanticEquality = CONDITIONAL not universally established [3m/300cm needs unit normalization; conceptual entities may need an ontology/identity registry]. ... IdentityConstruction can be computable, while IdentityResolution may rem
rows.statement: Equality, identity, and provenance are each split into a computable mechanical half and a conditional/non-computable semantic half: structural equality is computable via canonicalization+hashing while semantic equality is only conditionally computable (domain-dependent, e.g. unit normalization for 3m vs 300cm); identity CONSTRUCTION (deterministic hashing of canonical data) is computable while identity RESOLUTION (whether two independently-supplied references denote the same real-world entity) may remain externally supplied or human-governed; provenance-reference LOOKUP is computable under three infrastructure assumptions, but this never establishes ProvenanceTruth — lookup is not validation.

rows.anchor: Replay = Conditionally Computable [K0 persisted; every Ti defined; every input available; operation versions fixed; preconditions satisfied; operations deterministic]. ... Replayability ⇒ Immutable or versioned transformation semantics. ... Replay ≠ Reversal. Replay means reconstructing the forward
rows.statement: Replay is conditionally computable under six named preconditions, and is proven to REQUIRE operation versioning (since changing an operation's semantics between (T1^2026) and (T1^2027) could replay the same history to different states, replayability implies immutable-or-versioned transformation semantics); Replay is also proven distinct from Reversal — if T is many-to-one (K1!=K2 but T(K1)=T(K2)), no inverse can uniquely reconstruct the original state, so Replay only reconstructs the forward computation, it does not recover an original state from an output.

rows.anchor: K* = coarsest sufficient state abstraction. But can we compute K*? In general, this is not automatically decidable. ... Minimality = NOT YET COMPUTABLY ESTABLISHED. This is not a defect in the theory. It is a correct research status. ... TestMinimal(K) [testing removals can discover counterexamples]
rows.statement: Minimality (computing the coarsest sufficient K*) is found NOT YET COMPUTABLY ESTABLISHED, explicitly classified as a correct research status rather than a defect, requiring five unmet conditions (candidate abstraction, complete operation set, defined equivalence relation, sufficiency proof, strict-reduction-breaks-sufficiency proof); a further distinction is drawn between TestMinimal(K) (removal testing, which can find counterexamples) and ProveMinimal(K) (a full proof), since finite removal testing can never prove no future operation will require a removed component — empirical minimality evidence is not a mathematical minimality proof.

rows.anchor: Governance decision = possibly non-computable input. ... Evidence handling is computable in layers [Retrieve(e), Hash(e), Link(A,e) computable; Assess(e,A) may require a human or statistical model]. ... rows.statement: A candidate 'Computability Boundary Principle' theorem is proposed: an operation T:X x C -> Y is computable relative to C if X,C,Y have effective representations, all preconditions are decidable, T is a terminating algorithm, and all external dependencies have deterministic interfaces; if T depends on an undefined judgment predicate, T is not computable until that predicate is formalized — generalized as Computability(T) requires Computability of all of T's semantic dependencies, explicitly flagged as a derived candidate, not yet a proven corpus theorem.

aliases: the self-governing-policy gap and its repair

sources.note: Book chapter III.8's ratified content: the recurring defect of an admission policy governed by nothing (sighted independently four times -- corpus Step 121, freeze decisions, the falsification pass's F-1, and the conformance pass's CF-003/stale-banner finding), repaired by stratifying policy-as-content (revisable knowledge at rest in K_t) from policy-in-force (versioned, changeable only by a governed DC-decision), formalized as invariant I-11 which closes a hole the falsification pass found in I-1; the constitutional layer's Chapter V is presented as an independently-arrived-at parallel.

rows.anchor: Unresolved items
rows.statement: OQ-10 (constitution banner synchronization) HELD by ruling; the stale-banner fact and its resolution are narrated in I.2 and II.4, noted here because this chapter cites sighting 4 (the conformance-pass sighting of the same failure mode). No chapter-local unresolved items beyond it.

rows.anchor: The deepest defect the programme ever found — four separate times
rows.statement: A system whose admission machinery is governed by a policy that nothing governs is the deepest defect the programme found, discovered independently four times; the ratified answer is stratification.

rows.anchor: Stratification: policy-as-content vs policy-in-force
rows.statement: Policy-as-content is knowledge content at rest inside K_t (admissible, discussable, revisable like any claim); policy-in-force is the approved, versioned policy that actually governs admission; the change between them is a DECISION under DC, approved through governance (BC_Governance), producing version N -> N+1.

rows.anchor: Invariant I-11 closes the I-1 hole
rows.statement: I-11: no in-force policy -- the AcceptancePolicy and the constitution included -- changes without a governed, versioned approval decision; self-modification of the in-force policy is excluded by construction, not by exhortation. I-11 closes the hole the falsification pass found in I-1: the Knower's ownership now reaches Determination through the governed policy chain instead of stopping short at an unowned policy object.

rows.anchor: The four sightings
rows.statement: Four independent appearances of the same failure mode, on both sides of the programme: (1) corpus Step 121 flagged a 'critical governance gap' -- the admission constitution unversioned and unowned; (2) the corpus's freeze decisions modified the model's own rules mid-flight with no governing act; (3) the falsification pass caught the synthesized model repeating the pattern (finding F-1); (4) the conformance pass found the implementation side's Constitution asserting ratification downstream of a stale PROPOSED banner -- the mildest form, later resolved when governance located the actual retrospective ratification act.

rows.anchor: The constitutional layer's Chapter V parallel
rows.statement: The constitutional layer's Chapter V is the same idea in constitutional form: engineering evolution free below the articles; amendment of the articles only by ratified act; no weakening. Two traditions, one stratification, arrived at independently.

rows.anchor: The policy governs itself — governedly
rows.statement: The AcceptancePolicy is itself a governed, versioned object: policy-as-content (admissible like any claim, at rest inside K_t) is distinguished from policy-in-force (the approved version that actually governs admission), and no in-force policy changes without a governed decision (I-11); mentioned here because admission is where its absence would corrupt first.

rows.statement: Lists III.8's five claims with grades: (1) stratification [FA]; (2) I-11 with grade shown [FA/RC]; (3) I-1 closure [FA]; (4) four sightings reported with sides identified [E/H]; (5) independent constitutional parallel [E]. Terminology: no 'validated'; 'constitution' lower-case when generic, named when the artifact.

V parallel -> Constitution v1.0, 3C CF-011 [E].

rows.anchor: The gap that kept returning
rows.statement: Step 121 found the self-governing-policy gap first on the formal side: the machinery of admission was governed by a policy that nothing versioned and no one owned ('critical governance gap', the record says). The era's own freeze decisions -- stopping parts of the model mid-flight with no governing act -- were the same disease in behavioral form. The falsification pass would later catch the synthesized model repeating it, and the conformance pass would find its mildest cousin on the repository side. Four sightings; III.8 tells what the ratified architecture did about it.

rows.anchor: PF-9 ... The source algebra (025f) establishes... authority as a CONTEXT-INDEXED PARTIAL ORDER... a THREE-OUTCOME vocabulary Resolved/Unresolved/Invalid... the boxed ESCALATION LAW UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance... None of these has a distinct ratified object; I-10/I-11 + the R-1 loop carry the load-bearing minimum.
rows.statement: PF-9: the governance algebra source material (025f, 042, 121) establishes authority as a context-indexed partial order, scope/temporal applicability as conflict preconditions, a resolution machinery (hierarchy, supersession, explicit exception), a three-outcome vocabulary (Resolved/Unresolved/Invalid), a boxed escalation law (UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance, with "knowing that something cannot be determined is itself a valid computed result"), an Instruction!=AuthorizedDecision distinction, an AI-non-override rule, a version-transition schema, and the recursive-governance claim that the Constitution is itself a member of AuthoritativeKnowledge -- none of which has a distinct ratified object; only I-10/I-11 plus the R-1 loop carry the load-bearing minimum in the ratified architecture.

rows.anchor: Take the AcceptancePolicy -- the object whose mis-layering caused more recorded trouble than any other. As content, a policy draft is L2 material... As the governor of admission, the policy-in-force is an L2 object with an L1 shadow: Article 3 forbids it to self-authorize, and invariant I-11 forbids it to change without a governed, versioned decision
rows.statement: Traces the AcceptancePolicy (the object whose mis-layering caused the most recorded trouble in the programme) through all five layers as a worked example: as content it is L2 material at rest in K_t; as the governor of admission it is an L2 object with an L1 shadow (Article 3 forbids self-authorization, I-11 forbids ungoverned change); any enforcement would be L4 code that must first consult the governance record; and the failure the layering prevents is the programme's most-sighted defect (the policy that governs while nothing governs it, sighted independently four times, per Chapter III.8).

rows.anchor: FOUR interlocking guards make the modification governed rather than wild: 1. Mode separation... 2. The change is a Decision under contract... 3. Versioning with a transition schema... 4. Recursive self-subjection... The governor is inside the governed store, not above it.
rows.statement: States the chapter's central answer to why self-modifying admission policy is not an uncontrolled system: four interlocking guards -- (1) mode separation (proposed policy is content only, force requires the approved in-force version; "a rule that is sort of in effect" is unrepresentable), (2) the change is a Decision under the full III.7 Decision-Contract machinery (no-averaging conjunction, Unknown->Block, Auth as an act, per A6), (3) versioning with a transition schema (change rationale, authority, effective date, superseded version, verification; forward-only supersession), and (4) recursive self-subjection (Constitution subset-of AuthoritativeKnowledge -- the governing documents obey their own provenance/authority/temporal-validity/traceability disciplines) -- making self-modification exist exactly once, as a narrow contract-guarded versioned human-authorized transition, with every other path a type error.

rows.anchor: Instruction: a human demands not-r against the constitution's r; if the human lacks override authority, EffectiveConclusion = r... AuthorizedDecision: an authorized governance authority explicitly grants an exception... an LLM asserting "this approval is not necessary" is AIOutput |- not-r, and unless backed by an authoritative source AND accepted through the governance mechanism, Binding(AIOutput) = False -- "AI output cannot directly override governance... a fundamental KnowledgeOS invariant."
rows.statement: States the governance algebra's distinction between two senses of "a human said so": Instruction (an unauthorized demand against constitutional r yields EffectiveConclusion=r; the instruction is recorded as Rejected/NonBinding, never silently acted on) versus AuthorizedDecision (an authorized governance authority explicitly grants an exception -- a different semantic category with a different result), boxed as "Instruction and AuthorizedDecision must never be one type"; extends this with the AI clause at full source strength -- an LLM asserting an approval is unnecessary is AIOutput implies not-r, and Binding(AIOutput)=False unless backed by an authoritative source and accepted through the governance mechanism -- identified as the fourth of four independently-stated instances of the same AI-authority boundary across the book (the ladder chapter, the Decision Contract chapter, the constitution's Article 6, and here).
invariants: AI output cannot directly override governance

As the governor of admission, the policy-in-force is an L2 object with an L1 shadow: Article 3 forbids it to self-authorize, and invariant I-11 forbids it to change without a governed, versioned decision
rationale_evidence.statement: Traces the AcceptancePolicy (the object whose mis-layering caused the most recorded trouble in the programme) through all five layers as a worked example: as content it is L2 material at rest in K_t; as the governor of admission it is an L2 object with an L1 shadow (Article 3 forbids self-authorization, I-11 forbids ungoverned change); any enforcement would be L4 code that must first consult the governance record; and the failure the layering prevents is the programme's most-sighted defect (the policy that governs while nothing governs it, sighted independently four times, per Chapter III.8).

rationale_evidence.anchor: FOUR interlocking guards make the modification governed rather than wild: 1. Mode separation... 2. The change is a Decision under contract... 3. Versioning with a transition schema... 4. Recursive self-subjection... The governor is inside the governed store, not above it.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the chapter's central answer to why self-modifying admission policy is not an uncontrolled system: four interlocking guards -- (1) mode separation (proposed policy is content only, force requires the approved in-force version; "a rule that is sort of in effect" is unrepresentable), (2) the change is a Decision under the full III.7 Decision-Contract machinery (no-averaging conjunction, Unknown->Block, Auth as an act, per A6), (3) versioning with a transition schema (change rationale, authority, effective date, superseded version, verification; forward-only supersession), and (4) recursive self-subjection (Constitution subset-of AuthoritativeKnowledge -- the governing documents obey their own provenance/authority/temporal-validity/traceability disciplines) -- making self-modification exist exactly once, as a narrow contract-guarded versioned human-authorized transition, with every other path a type error.

rationale_evidence.anchor: the implementation-side constitution's "stale banner" turned out to mask a REAL ratification act, found by governance investigation -- the mildest form of the defect (tracking, not absence), and a live demonstration of why guard 3's recorded version transitions matter: an act that exists but is not carried on the artifact reproduces half the original disease.
rationale_evidence.statement: Resolves the fourth of the four independent sightings of the self-referential-policy defect: the implementation-side constitution's stale in-force banner was found by governance investigation to mask a real (but untracked) ratification act -- the mildest form of the defect, since the act existed but was not carried on the artifact -- offered as a live demonstration of why guard 3 (recorded version-transition tracking) matters, since an untracked-but-real act still reproduces half the original disease.

rows.anchor: Dimension | R1 -- Measure Theory Crisis | R2 -- Question/Lens | R3 -- Gita/Sarathi | R4 -- Computational Closure | R5 -- Step Construction/Reality.
rows.statement: The Step 238 master R1-R5 matrix populates 9 dimensions (approx period, primary question, dominant method, main object, mathematical role, DDD role, evidence status, major result, main danger) for each of the 5 epistemic regimes -- R1's primary question 'can KnowledgeOS be given a mathematical foundation', R2's 'what questions must be answered', R3's 'who/what owns the frame of knowledge/action', R4's 'can propositions be made computationally closed', R5's 'what does the architecture actually consist of'.

rows.anchor: Measure theory was abandoned as the foundational architecture. The corpus explicitly records the abandonment as ALT-01.
rows.statement: R1 (Measure Theory Crisis) is the cleanest historical episode: knowledge was initially imagined as a measurable structure with sigma-algebra machinery, but the substrate rapidly failed to represent the intended object and was explicitly abandoned as the foundational architecture, tracked as ALT-01.

rows.anchor: \Omega_a\rightarrow IdealState/contract, \Omega_b\rightarrow dropped, \Omega_c\rightarrow complement principle. ... X_t\neq Observed(X_t) as the surviving invariant I-7.
rows.statement: Despite R1's abandonment, Omega did not simply disappear: its three roles diverged into Omega_a->IdealState/contract, Omega_b->dropped, Omega_c->complement principle, with the latter producing the surviving invariant I-7 (X_t != Observed(X_t)) -- an example of architectural evolution through failed formalization.

rows.anchor: Omega first appears in the kernel era, 2026-08-24. ... R1 transformed Omega; R1 did not create Omega.
rows.statement: Important correction: Omega did not originate in R1 as previously assumed -- it first appears in the kernel era (2026-08-24), in Bayesian/typed mathematical work, BEFORE the measure-theory phase begins (August 25); R1 transformed Omega, it did not create it.

rows.anchor: Foundation\rightarrow Questions. ... The question series should therefore not be treated as merely another collection of philosophical essays. It represents a change in epistemic method.
rows.statement: R2 is characterized as changing instruments after R1's failure (Foundation->Questions) while retaining the demand for rigor -- the Question series represents a genuine change in epistemic method, not merely a collection of philosophical essays.

rows.anchor: Gita\rightarrow Interpretation not: Gita\rightarrow Mathematical theorem. ... Knower owns the frame as the Sarathi invariant. ... Kshetrajna is reported as the only concept found both in the formal corpus and repository constitution under the same Sanskrit lineage.
rows.statement: R3 (Gita/Sarathi) introduces the 'Knower owns the frame' Sarathi invariant, notable because Kshetrajna is reported as the only concept found both in the formal mathematical corpus and the repository constitution under the same Sanskrit lineage -- materially stronger than a generic analogy, but still classified as historical evidence of conceptual lineage, not mathematical derivation; the governing rule remains Gita->Interpretation, never Gita->MathematicalTheorem.

rows.anchor: Zero with three historically distinct senses: 1. absence-lens Zero; 2. goal-gap Zero(K,G,EC); 3. repository neutral-reference principle. ... Lord has two unresolved referents: Omega-observer versus action selector. ... Same word\neq Same concept.
rows.statement: R3 also introduces semantic collisions: 'Zero' carries three historically distinct senses (absence-lens Zero, goal-gap Zero(K,G,EC), repository neutral-reference principle) and 'Lord' has two unresolved referents (Omega-observer vs action selector, explicitly marked unresolved by the corpus itself) -- an important DDD lesson: same word does not imply same concept.

rows.anchor: ComputationalClosure\neq EmpiricalValidation. ... no actual interpreter invocations, command execution, test-runner output, or measured quantities across the large claimed experiment region. ... formalization toward computational testability rather than empirically validated computational theory.
rows.statement: R4 (Computational Closure) attempts to render conceptual principles (Invariant, Predicate, Transformation, Closure) computationally expressible, but the audit found zero actual interpreter invocations/command execution/test-runner output/measured quantities across the claimed experiment region -- ComputationalClosure != EmpiricalValidation; R4 must be described as formalization toward computational testability, not an empirically validated computational theory.

rows.anchor: later steps dropped earlier statistical machinery; notation changed; earlier causal/identifiability structure disappeared; some hash-chain mechanisms weakened; concepts were simplified without explicit supersession. ... Step succession does not imply semantic preservation.
rows.statement: R5 (Sequential architecture construction) introduces the methodological hazard that S_{n+1} may silently simplify or mutate S_n, with concrete documented examples (dropped statistical machinery, changed notation, disappeared causal/identifiability structure, weakened hash-chain mechanisms, simplification without explicit supersession) -- Step succession does not imply semantic preservation.

rows.anchor: What actually exists in the software, artifacts, processes and runtime mechanisms? rather than merely: What should KnowledgeOS contain? ... Model\neq Reality.
rows.statement: R5's decisive methodological turn is identified at Step 109, shifting from 'what should KnowledgeOS contain' to 'what actually exists in the software/artifacts/processes/runtime mechanisms' -- approaching the distinction Model != Reality.

rows.anchor: Step 158 calls itself a reality test, but the subsequent audit found: 0 repository paths; 0 inspection results; no actual reality inspection; multiple boxed conclusions. ... DeclaredRealityTest\neq ExecutedRealityTest. ... perhaps the single most important methodological lesson from the entire archa
rows.statement: R5 nevertheless contains a serious contradiction: Step 158 calls itself a reality test yet the audit found zero repository paths, zero inspection results, and no actual reality inspection despite multiple boxed conclusions -- DeclaredRealityTest != ExecutedRealityTest, rated perhaps the single most important methodological lesson from the entire archaeology.

rows.anchor: R1: Choose a mathematical foundation ... R5: Construct and test against reality. This is a methodological evolution, not necessarily a sequence of increasingly correct architectures.
rows.statement: The five regimes form an epistemic ladder R1(choose foundation)->R2(question foundations)->R3(introduce interpretive lenses)->R4(make claims formally computable)->R5(construct and test against reality) -- explicitly a methodological evolution, not necessarily a sequence of increasingly correct architectures.

rows.anchor: R3\rightarrow R4. ... What justified this formalization? ... A=justification exists elsewhere; B=implicit experiment; C=explicit hypothesis; D=creative modelling move; E=still unvalidated. ... this bridge must not be repaired retrospectively.
rows.statement: The critical missing bridge is the R3->R4 transition (philosophical/conceptual lens -> formal mathematical object): the corpus itself asks what justified this formalization, listing 5 possible explanations (justification exists elsewhere, implicit experiment, explicit hypothesis, creative modelling move, still unvalidated) and explicitly states this bridge must not be repaired retrospectively.

rows.anchor: R1=Gather, R2=Adjudicate, R3=Custody, R4=Contemporaneity, R5=Separability. But these are not yet five bounded contexts. ... R5 is explicitly described as cross-cutting rather than a standalone responsibility.
rows.statement: DDD interpretation of the regimes identifies 5 distinct responsibility themes (Gather, Adjudicate, Custody, Contemporaneity, Separability -- confusingly also labeled R1-R5, colliding with the epistemic-regime numbering) not yet demonstrated as five bounded contexts (R5/Separability is explicitly cross-cutting); 'evidence' itself changes meaning between collection, adjudication, custody and contemporaneity -- exactly what DDD predicts when one term hides multiple models.

rows.anchor: Evidence_C where C=semantic context. Meaning(Evidence,C_1)\neq Meaning(Evidence,C_2) may be entirely legitimate. This is where DDD and the mathematical theory can genuinely meet.
rows.statement: The mathematical architecture should model semantic context explicitly: rather than a bare Evidence, use Evidence_C (context-parameterized), allowing Meaning(Evidence,C1) != Meaning(Evidence,C2) as entirely legitimate -- the point where DDD and mathematical theory genuinely meet.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS=Knowledge+Context+Evidence+State+Transformation+Authority+Lineage subject to: No component is canonical merely because a later Step names it.
rows.statement: First convergence hypothesis: a candidate architecture KnowledgeOS = Knowledge+Context+Evidence+State+Transformation+Authority+Lineage, subject to the constraint that no component is canonical merely because a later step names it -- each must be traced back to historical evidence + domain semantics + software evidence.

rows.anchor: \mathcal K_8=(E,S,T,O,P,R,\Pi,A) and the later proposed \mathfrak K_5=(G,\sigma,\theta,\lambda,\pi). We must now determine whether K_8\cong K_5 or merely K_5 is a later compression of K_8. ... K_5 loses distinctions present in K_8.
rows.statement: What happened to the original mathematical kernel: three possible relationships between the earlier 8-component kernel mathcal K_8=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) and the later 5-component mathfrak K_5=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) are posed -- isomorphic, K_5 a later compression of K_8, or K_5 losing distinctions present in K_8 (flagged as particularly important given the archaeology has already demonstrated semantic loss between later steps).

rows.anchor: \rho:\mathcal K_8\rightarrow\mathfrak K_5. ... Injective ... Surjective ... Bijective ... SemanticLoss(\rho)=?
rows.statement: This is formalized as a genuine mathematical question via a candidate reduction map rho:K_8->K_5 tested for injectivity (no primitive distinction lost), surjectivity (every K_5 component has a historical predecessor), and bijectivity (equivalent information), with the central open question SemanticLoss(rho)=?, connecting directly to the repaired semantic-integrity framework.

rows.anchor: \mathcal C(K_1)\subseteq Recoverable(\rho(K_1))\cup DeclaredLoss(\rho). This is precisely the kind of mathematical architecture we can defend.
rows.statement: A possible formal criterion for kernel-reduction adequacy: a reduction rho:K1->K2 is semantically adequate iff C(K1) (critical semantic distinctions of the historical kernel) subseteq Recoverable(rho(K1)) union DeclaredLoss(rho) -- directly reusing the repaired semantic-integrity apparatus for the kernel-reduction problem itself.

rows.anchor: R_1\ldots R_5 are epistemic regimes, not architectural layers. ... Foundation\rightarrow Question\rightarrow Interpretation\rightarrow Formalization\rightarrow Reality. ... A formalization does not become architecture until its semantic and empirical status is established.
rows.statement: Step 238 verdict: the five-regime model is sufficiently supported as a historical framework, with the explicit qualification that R1..R5 are epistemic regimes, not architectural layers; the most important historical trajectory is Foundation->Question->Interpretation->Formalization->Reality, and the most important methodological rule is that a formalization does not become architecture until its semantic and empirical status is established.

notations: EC_t → Req(EC_t) → r → Eval → EvalReq → Sat → Δ_t → Zero → Det → Decision → Authorization → Action

sources.note: A 2026-09-10 mathematical_ideas-lane document claiming a complete twelve-node corpus derivation chain from EC_t to Action, self-declaring Sat/Eval/EvalReq/Det/Det_r/Decision each DEFINED/CORPUS-SUPPORTED and narrowing open gaps to standard-semantics/Det_r-responsibility/Sat-F4-validation/EC-reconciliation/Gamma-bridge plus three missing F4 instantiations. Markedly more optimistic than the concurrent gap-discovery lane (same batch) on the identical Sat/EvalReq/Det_r objects; self-declared statuses treated as claims per corpus-reliability caution.

rows.anchor: The most important correction is: Sat, Eval, Det, Req, r, Δ and parts of EC are not simply 'undefined.' Their derivation exists in the corpus. What remains open is whether the latest derivation is valid, internally coherent, and legitimately the F4/canonical lineage.
rows.statement: Argues, against a prior 'missing concepts' assessment, that Sat, Eval, Det, Req, r, Delta and parts of EC are not simply undefined -- their derivations already exist somewhere in the corpus -- and reframes the open question from 'where is the definition' to 'is the existing derivation valid, internally coherent, and legitimately the F4/canonical lineage.' Presented as this document's own re-assessment claim.

rows.anchor: The actual derivation chain ... EC_t → Req(EC_t) → r → Eval → EvalReq → Sat → Δ_t → Zero → Det → Decision → Authorization → Action ... The reconstructed dependency graph explicitly records this sequence and its source locations.
rows.statement: Asserts a complete twelve-node corpus derivation chain EC_t -> Req(EC_t) -> r -> Eval -> EvalReq -> Sat -> Delta_t -> Zero -> Det -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action, claiming a 'reconstructed dependency graph' explicitly records this sequence with source locations for each edge. Presented as this document's own reconstruction claim; the underlying dependency graph/ledger it cites is not itself included in this batch.

rows.anchor: 2. Req is actually derived ... R_I → R → Req(EC_t) ... r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity). The corpus classifies r as CORPUS-SUPPORTED, DEFINED.
rows.statement: Claims r is derived through a chain R_I -> R -> Req(EC_t), with r in Req(EC_t) given a 7-field structure r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity), self-described as 'the corpus classifies r as CORPUS-SUPPORTED, DEFINED' -- extracted as a self-declared classification, not verified fact. Revises the document's own earlier position that r was 'merely structurally unclear' to 'r=DEFINED', with a remaining open issue around the semantics of its 'standard' field.

rows.anchor: 3. EC_t is derived—but has two surviving versions ... EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t) ... EC=⟨Req,Rules,Scope,EvidenceRequirements,TemporalRequirements,AuthorityRequirements⟩. The corpus explicitly classifies these as same lineage but non-identical, unreconciled structures.
rows.statement: Records two surviving EC_t structures -- an early 4-argument canonical form EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t) and a later 6-component structure <Req,Rules,Scope,EvidenceRequirements,TemporalRequirements,AuthorityRequirements> -- self-described as classified by the corpus as 'same lineage but non-identical, unreconciled structures.' Concludes EC_t is defined but its canonical identity is unresolved, distinguishing this from 'EC is undefined.'

rows.anchor: 4. standard is genuinely still missing ... r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity) but its mathematical body is never supplied. ... Policy_Det(p)= {Established if sufficient independent support; Rejected if sufficient challenge; Conflicted if unresolved conflict; Unknown otherwise} ... the exact policy belongs to the epistemic contract. ... standard: responsibility visible, semantics incomplete. This is probably the smallest genuine semantic gap in this area.
rows.statement: Identifies r's 'standard' field as a genuine, still-open gap: named in r's structure but its mathematical body never supplied anywhere. Traces a partial responsibility chain (standard -> EC.Rules/epistemic contract -> Policy_Det -> sufficiency/challenge) via a cited Policy_Det(p) four-branch classification (Established/Rejected/Conflicted/Unknown based on sufficient support/challenge/conflict), itself stating 'the exact policy belongs to the epistemic contract.' Concludes: responsibility for 'standard' is visible but its semantics remain incomplete -- judged 'probably the smallest genuine semantic gap in this area.'

rows.anchor: 5. Eval is actually fully derived ... Eval(K,p,Γ,EC) = ⟨E_p,J_p,U_p,C_p,S_p⟩ ... Eval: K×E×P×EC×Γ → 𝒱 ... The corpus explicitly marks this as CORPUS-SUPPORTED, DEFINED. ... Eval ≠ missing. ... The remaining issue is whether it is the right F4 evaluator.
rows.statement: Claims Eval is 'actually fully derived,' presenting an intermediate 5-tuple Eval(K,p,Gamma,EC)=<E_p,J_p,U_p,C_p,S_p> and a fuller signature Eval:KxExPxECxGamma->V with output vector v=<Support,CounterSupport,Uncertainty,Conflict,Dependencies,Assumptions,Justification>, self-described as marked CORPUS-SUPPORTED/DEFINED. Concludes Eval is not missing, with the remaining open question being whether it is the RIGHT evaluator for F4 specifically.

rows.anchor: 6. EvalReq is derived ... EvalReq(K,r,EC,Γ) as depending on Eval and r. So: Eval → EvalReq. This is important because it means the later Sat definition is not floating in isolation.
rows.statement: Claims EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma) is derived as depending on Eval and r (Eval -> EvalReq edge), arguing this matters because it grounds the later Sat definition rather than leaving it isolated.

rows.anchor: 7. And now the major correction: Sat actually has a derived computational body ... Sat(K,r,Γ) = Det_r(EvalReq(K,r,EC,Γ),EC) from [05-41], Definition 6.18. ... the only file in the entire 876-file traversal that supplies a computable body for Sat in terms of independently typed inputs. ... two proved theorems rest on this definition. ... Sat has a corpus-derived computational definition. But: Sat has not been adversarially validated/ratified.
rows.statement: Presents as its major correction that Sat has a derived computational body: Sat(K,r,Gamma)=Det_r(EvalReq(K,r,EC,Gamma),EC), cited to a specific source '[05-41] Definition 6.18', self-described as 'the only file in the entire 876-file traversal that supplies a computable body for Sat in terms of independently typed inputs,' with two theorems claimed to rest on it. Concludes Sat has a corpus-derived computational definition but has NOT been adversarially validated or ratified -- framing 'Defined != Validated' as the now-central distinction. Note: this directly parallels but is markedly more optimistic than the concurrent gap-discovery lane's (S2907-S2919) finding that EvalReq/Det_r lack established operational semantics and Det_r is 97% firewalled with only one readable definitional source; both cite the same or a closely related boxed Sat=Det_r(EvalReq(...),EC) formula but reach different conclusions about how much is actually established.

rows.anchor: 8. The derivation of Sat can be reconstructed explicitly ... Sat = Det_r ∘ EvalReq ∘ Eval subject to the exact argument dependencies. The dependency ledger confirms precisely this structure. That is a derivation, not merely a naming convention.
rows.statement: Presents Sat's derivation explicitly as a function composition Sat = Det_r o EvalReq o Eval (subject to argument dependencies), claiming a 'dependency ledger' confirms exactly this structure, and asserting this constitutes a genuine derivation rather than merely a naming convention.

rows.anchor: 9. Δ_t is completely derived from Sat ... Δ_t = {r∈Req(EC_t):¬Sat(K_t,r)}. ... Sat → Δ_t. ... two historical senses of Δ_t, which the corpus classifies as a harmless homonym rather than a fundamental missing concept.
rows.statement: Claims Delta_t is completely derived from Sat via Delta_t={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)}, appearing (per this document) in both the canonical theory and a later dependency graph, establishing a Sat->Delta_t edge. Notes two historical senses of Delta_t exist but are self-classified by the corpus as a harmless homonym rather than a fundamental missing concept.

rows.anchor: 10. Zero is derived—but there are competing branches ... Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t=∅. ... ZeroLens(K_t,Γ_t,L_t) → Boundary_t. ... these are branch-local alternatives; the later [05-36]–[05-40] lineage continues using Δ=∅. ... Zero has mathematical derivations, but its canonical semantic identity is branch-dependent.
rows.statement: Finds two competing Zero derivations: an early-canonical-theory proved theorem Zero(K_t,EC_t) iff Delta_t=empty-set (giving Sat->Delta->Zero), versus an alternative branch ZeroLens(K_t,Gamma_t,L_t)->Boundary_t; self-describes the corpus as explicitly warning these are branch-local alternatives, with a later [05-36]-[05-40] lineage continuing to use the Delta=empty-set reading. Concludes Zero has mathematical derivations but its canonical semantic identity is branch-dependent, distinguishing this from 'Zero is undefined.'

rows.anchor: 11. Det is also derived ... Det(K,p,EC,Γ) ⟺ ∀r∈Req_p(EC,Γ), Sat(K,r)=Satisfied. ... Det⇒Δ_p=∅. ... the Determination-Gap Equivalence theorem. ... Det is not merely a signature. It has a body.
rows.statement: Claims Det(K,p,EC,Gamma) is defined as a universally-quantified requirement-satisfaction predicate (iff every requirement in Req_p(EC,Gamma) is Satisfied under Sat), with a claimed proved corollary Det=>Delta_p=empty-set and a named 'Determination-Gap Equivalence theorem.' Concludes Det has a full body, not merely a signature -- though notes 'the subtle remaining problem is Det_r' specifically.

rows.anchor: 12. Det_r is where the real semantic responsibility problem moves ... object-level Det_r/EvalReq are defined; their responsibility lineage is not fully established; Policy_Det is the closest same-document candidate; but it is only an illustrative template. ... What mathematically determines Det_r? That is much narrower than: 'Is Det_r defined?' The latter is largely answered.
rows.statement: Narrows the open Det_r question: claims object-level Det_r/EvalReq ARE defined (self-declared, contradicting the concurrent gap-discovery lane's finding that Det_r's body is 'nowhere readable' and 97% firewalled), but their RESPONSIBILITY LINEAGE (what determines which specific standing Det_r returns) is not fully established -- Policy_Det is identified as the closest same-document candidate but is 'only an illustrative template,' not a completed mechanism. Reframes the question from 'is Det_r defined' (claimed largely answered here) to the narrower 'what mathematically determines Det_r.'

rows.anchor: 13. Standing(p) is a real predecessor—but must not be silently substituted ... Σ={Unknown,Supported,Refuted} as a minimal candidate epistemic state ... Evidence → Assessment → Standing(p) which may potentially discharge some of the responsibility later assigned to Det_r. But governance correctly did not adopt Standing as a substitute. So this is a candidate bridge, not a completed bridge.
rows.statement: Identifies an independently executed Standing(p) evaluator using Sigma={Unknown,Supported,Refuted} (with Conflicted derivable rather than primitive) as a real predecessor object, proposing a candidate bridge Evidence -> Assessment -> Standing(p) that could potentially discharge some of Det_r's responsibility -- but notes governance correctly did not adopt Standing as a substitute for Det_r, so this remains a candidate bridge, not a completed one, and warns against silently substituting it.

rows.anchor: 14. Decision is derived separately ... Decision = f(Determination, DecisionRule/Policy) ... Determination ⇏ Decision. The dependency graph states this explicitly. That is important because it validates the separation we developed in the Action Fact-Finding work.
rows.statement: Claims Decision is derived as Decision=f(Determination, DecisionRule/Policy), with a proved non-implication result Determination does-not-imply Decision explicitly stated in a cited dependency graph. Frames this as validating a separate, prior 'Action Fact-Finding' work's development of the Determination/Decision distinction (connecting to this batch's earlier action-rationale-and-why-act-factfinding object from B0068).

lineage_claims.quote: That is important because it validates the separation we developed in the Action Fact-Finding work.

rows.anchor: 15. The complete derivation ... reconstructed mathematical skeleton (ASCII pipeline diagram EC_t → Req(EC_t) → r → {Evidence, standard} → Eval → EvalReq → Det_r → Sat(K,r,Γ) → Δ_t → Zero → Determination → Decision → Authorization → Action → Observation/K_{t+1})
rows.statement: Draws a full reconstructed pipeline diagram: EC_t -> Req(EC_t) -> r, branching into Evidence and standard, both feeding through Eval -> EvalReq -> Det_r -> Sat(K,r,Gamma) -> Delta_t -> Zero -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Observation/K_{t+1}, claiming this graph is 'directly supported by the corpus reconstruction.'

rows.anchor: 16. What is genuinely still missing? G1 — standard/acceptance semantics ... G2 — Det_r responsibility semantics ... G1→G2. G3 — F4 validity of the complete Sat construction ... Defined ≠ Validated. G4 — EC_t canonical reconciliation ... G5 — Γ identity/responsibility bridge
rows.statement: Narrows the genuinely unresolved list to five items: G1 the mathematical criterion for 'sufficient support'/'sufficient challenge' underlying standard/acceptance semantics (the narrowest genuine gap); G2 Det_r's responsibility semantics (what makes it return one standing rather than another), explicitly dependent on G1 (G1->G2); G3 the F4 adversarial validity of the complete Sat construction Sat=Det_r(EvalReq(...),EC), framed via the central distinction Defined != Validated; G4 EC_t's canonical reconciliation between its two structured versions (an identity problem, not an incompleteness problem); G5 Gamma's identity/responsibility bridge, reclassified as SUBDIVIDED rather than four competing meanings, with the unresolved point being how the bare Gamma in EvalReq maps to later subdivisions.

rows.anchor: 17. And three things are genuinely absent: F4 Observation semantics ... Obs_{F4}(K) ... NOT FOUND. F4 Behaviour semantics ... Beh_{F4}(K) ... no construction exists. F4 Trace semantics ... Tr_{F4}(K) ... no instance exists. These are not merely 'validation gaps.' They are missing F4 instantiations.
rows.statement: Identifies three items as genuinely, flatly absent rather than merely unvalidated: an F4-specific instantiation Obs_F4(K) of the abstract Obs_{Q,O}(K) observation framework (self-described as explicitly 'NOT FOUND' in the corpus); an F4-specific behavior construction Beh_F4(K) (no construction exists at all); and an F4-specific trace instance Tr_F4(K) (the abstract Trace framework exists but no F4 instance does). Distinguishes these from 'validation gaps' -- they are missing INSTANTIATIONS, a different category.

rows.anchor: 18. Therefore the correct mathematical status is (status table for K_t, EC_t, Req, r, standard, Eval, EvalReq, Sat, Det_r, Det, Standing, Δ_t, Zero, Decision, Γ, F4 Obs/Beh/Trace, F4 semantic equivalence, F3↔F4 bridge)

notations: k_t = smallest independently evaluable knowledge claim about an observation
aliases: Kt smallest unit of knowledge about an observation

sources.note: Extended iterative dialogue (S2309) developing the candidate definition 'K_t is the smallest possible epistemically meaningful unit of knowledge about an observation o at time t', worked through a repeated Nexus-server example (ten independent statements = ten candidate knowledge dimensions/units), with the caveats that a sentence is a linguistic representation that may contain one or more K_t units, that the number of sentences gives a possible but not necessarily true dimensional view, that K_t(O) subset-of all potentially observable aspects of O (Knowledge at t != the complete observation), and that a minimality criterion is proposed operationally as: if K_t can be decomposed into smaller units without losing knowledge about the observation, it wasn't minimal. Explicitly frozen only as a candidate/hypothesis with eight open questions (what is an observation; what makes a unit epistemically meaningful; what does smallest mean formally; can K_t be decomposed; does K_t's identity persist under change; K_t's relation to evidence/justification/context/authority; is K_t necessarily time-indexed; can two representations describe the same K_t).

rows.anchor: K_t is the smallest possible unit of knowledge about an observation at time t.
rows.statement: Proposes, and repeatedly re-affirms as a 'candidate definition, not yet formally proven', K_t(o) = the smallest epistemically meaningful unit of knowledge about observation o at time t, explicitly warning against prematurely identifying K_t with a data point, a claim, or the existing six-tuple (entity/property/context/relation/time/authority) -- those may become representations of K_t, not K_t itself, restated as the invariant 'Representation != Knowledge Identity'.

rows.anchor: Can K_t be decomposed into smaller knowledge units without losing the knowledge about the observation? If yes, it wasn't minimal. If no, we have a candidate minimal knowledge unit.
rows.statement: Proposes an operational minimality criterion for K_t via a decomposition test (K_t -> {K_t,1, K_t,2, ...}): if the decomposition preserves all knowledge about the observation, the original unit was not minimal; if no such decomposition exists, it is a candidate minimal unit -- offered as a way to formalize 'smallest' without prematurely fixing K_t's internal structure.

rows.anchor: A sentence is a linguistic representation that may contain one or more K_t units. ... the number of sentences gives us a possible dimensional view, but not necessarily the true number of dimensions.
rows.statement: Using a repeated Nexus-server worked example (RHEL 9.8, 8 vCPU, port 8081, etc. as ten atomic statements), argues a sentence is not necessarily one K_t unit -- e.g. 'has 8 vCPUs and 31 GB RAM' contains two atomic units -- and that an observation's true dimensionality is not bounded by however many sentences currently describe it (K_t(O) subset-of all potentially observable aspects of O; 'Knowledge at t != the complete observation'); new sentences discovered later add new dimensions (K_t^11), and a corrected statement changes an existing dimension's value rather than necessarily creating a new one.

rows.anchor: WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution, with history H_{<=t} preserved. It then proposes K_t^{A,R} as a time-indexed knowledge attribution, dependent on participant A, extraction regime R.
rows.statement: Reading an unread-in-this-batch corpus document, reports its chain WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution (with preserved history H_{<=t}) and its participant/regime-relative K_t^{A,R}; explicitly distinguishes this from the dialogue's own new atomic-K_t hypothesis, treating the latter as a possible FURTHER refinement (one measurable statement per observation dimension) rather than something the attached document already established, and notes the document's own probability treatment P(K_t^A|F_t^A) as extraction-uncertainty, explicitly distinct from Knowledge itself.

rows.anchor: Q = domain of possible items; K subset-of Q = a particular knowledge state; script-K = space/family of possible states; probability (Q, script-K, p). The crucial distinction is: script-K != K_t != P(K_t | O_{<=t}).
rows.statement: Reports a Knowledge Space Theory (KST) formalism (Q as domain of possible items, K as a particular state, script-K as the family of possible states, with probability attached as (Q,script-K,p)) as external confirmation that a knowledge-space, a particular state, and a probability distribution over states are three genuinely different objects; notes KST's own K_t is a learner-capability state (a different, narrower sense than the dialogue's broader KnowledgeOS K_t), and that the dialogue's atomic-unit idea asks a question KST does not answer: what is the state/value of each individual knowledge unit within a state.

rows.anchor: P(k_i | E) is the epistemic confidence/degree of support for proposition k_i, given the available evidence. ... k_i != P(k_i)
rows.statement: Repeatedly insists that probability attached to a knowledge unit must be given a precise referent -- distinguishing P(claim is true), P(claim is supported by available evidence), P(the measurement/extraction is correct), and P(claim belongs to K_t) as not necessarily the same quantity, and stating k_i != P(k_i): the knowledge unit itself is not identical to its probability. Also proposes that not every claim's epistemic measure need be a probability -- it could be categorical status, an interval, a confidence level, measurement uncertainty, or logical entailment strength -- warning against forcing every kind of knowledge into probability merely because probability is mathematically convenient.

rows.anchor: Observation -> Atomic propositions -> Evidence -> Measured epistemic state -> Ideal/reference state -> distance -> knowledge gap. This potentially connects several previously separate strands: Phase 1 ... Phase 2 ... KST ... Pritchard ... Zero ... Knower ... Evidence ... Kernel
rows.statement: Proposes a 'candidate unifying structure, not yet a completed theory': Observation -> Atomic propositions -> Evidence -> Measured epistemic state -> Ideal/reference state -> distance -> knowledge gap, claimed to potentially connect the corpus's Phase-1 (knowledge as relationship/justification/state evolution), Phase-2 (Knowledge Space/participant/time/projection), KST (Q, script-K, K_t, p), Pritchard's belief-counts-as-knowledge conditions, Zero, Knower-ownership, Evidence/determination, and Kernel-as-substrate strands, while explicitly warning against collapsing these prematurely.

rows.anchor: EpistemicState = Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity
rows.statement: Reports a multidimensional EpistemicState formulation (Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity) as already-derived corpus material supporting the general direction of a non-monolithic, multi-axis knowledge state, alongside a stated distinction chain Knowledge!=Reality, Observation!=Knowledge, Dimension!=Statement, Dimension!=Value, Guidance!=Decision, Zero!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Dimension-Discovery.

rows.anchor: What is the minimum structure of k_t such that the entire KnowledgeOS theory — evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision and action — can be derived without adding arbitrary architectural assumptions?
rows.statement: Closes the file's line of inquiry with an explicit unresolved research question: what is the minimal structure of the atomic knowledge unit k_t from which the rest of the theory (evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision, action) could be derived without arbitrary additional architectural assumptions -- stated as the next major research question rather than answered.

rows.anchor: A sentence is not automatically a knowledge dimension merely because it is syntactically a sentence. ... independent knowledge-bearing statement -> candidate dimension
rows.statement: Restates the minimal-knowledge-unit hypothesis k_t(O) (smallest independently meaningful unit of knowledge about an observation at t) with the qualification that sentence != dimension automatically -- semantic independence of a statement must be established before it counts as a candidate dimension; and states K_t(O) is necessarily partial, since K_t(O) subset-of D(O), the full (possibly unbounded) dimension set of the observation.

rows.anchor: k_i = (O, d_i, v_i, t, E_i, p_i, q_i)
rows.statement: Extends the atomic knowledge claim to a seven-field tuple k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,p_i,q_i) -- observation, semantic dimension, claimed value, time, evidence/information source, epistemic probability, and an explicit information-sufficiency/support status q_i -- with K_t(O)={k_1,...,k_n} as the resulting knowledge state, and reiterates that dimensionality is representation-relative rather than an intrinsic finite property of the object (a sentence maps to one or more atomic claims, not one-to-one).

rows.anchor: K_t should not be identified with a Kripke model or possible-world set. Status: research conclusion / compatibility constraint, not yet kernel theorem.
rows.statement: Confirms the DEL document's rejection of K_t as a Kripke pointed model (M,w) strengthens (without proving) the corpus's independently-developed atomic-tuple direction k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,C_i,p_i,q_i); explicitly records the possible-worlds rejection as a research conclusion/compatibility constraint, not a kernel theorem.
